Subtract the Sewers scene relocation base from every split scene pointer, then retire this one-shot routine
Inputs: $4C52 = pointer count; $4C53/$4C54 = 16-bit relocation base; split pointers at $4C95/$4C96 for indices below $80 and $4D95/$4D96 for indices $80 and above
Outputs: every selected pointer is rewritten in place; on completion opcode $60 is written at $759F so later calls immediately return
Clobbers: A, X, flags, and $1E; Y is preserved

Where the relocation loop really starts. As the level is loaded, $759F-$75A0 hold LDA #$00, so the count at $1E starts from zero here; once every pointer is done, $75AA-$75AC write RTS ($60) over that LDA, so in a snapshot taken during play $759F reads RTS and $75A0 keeps the old $00.

Inputs: area index $A2; area root table $4C55; background table $4C56; relocated split scene pointers $4C95/$4C96 and $4D95/$4D96; the scene base $4C52, added to the pointer as the immediates #$E4/#$4D at $760D and $7612
Outputs: root pointer $02/$03 and renderer bounds/depth/offset state are initialized; recursive records are traversed and their leaves update bitmap, screen, and color work memory
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, recursive stack use, scene pointers and renderer scratch including $02/$03, $0A, $1A/$1B, $38, $DC, and $E7
Hardware: directly writes VIC-II background color $D021; the leaf renderer at $76D9 writes the bitmap, screen RAM, colour RAM and the colour copy at $0800 itself; only for a cell whose colour copy already has bits 5-7 set does it look further, leaving the cell alone when the new colour byte is below $20 and calling the resident compositor ($1411, which jumps to $17F6) when that byte has bit 4 set

Render room A in the Sewers playable phase, entering the normal scene renderer after its usual load from $A2.
Inputs: A is a valid room index; relocated scene pointers, renderer workspace, bitmap/screen/color buffers, and the active phase are initialized.
Outputs: Selects the room's scene pointer, writes its background color to $D021, traverses the scene-record tree, and renders the room.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, processor flags, $02-$05, renderer scratch, and VIC-II-visible bitmap/screen/color work memory.
Hardware: Writes VIC-II background-color register $D021 and display memory; no CIA access.

Interpret and render a scene-record tree. Inputs: $02/$03 record pointer and initialized renderer workspace. Outputs: bitmap, screen, color, and traversal state are updated. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and renderer zero-page scratch. Hardware: changes hardware-visible bitmap, screen, and color RAM; no direct VIC-II register write is required.

Dispatch the current encoded scene record for the Sewers playable phase, restoring a parent record at nested terminators and returning at the outer terminator.
Inputs: $02/$03 point at the current record; $1A/$1B hold the composite origin; $38 is nesting depth; nested parent frames are on the stack.
Outputs: Decodes nonterminal records; $FF at depth zero returns, while nested $FF restores the parent frame, advances $02/$03, and continues dispatch.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, processor flags, $02-$05, $1A/$1B, $25/$26, $38, renderer scratch, and restored stack bytes.
Hardware: No direct register write here; descendant rendering changes VIC-II-visible bitmap, screen-code, and color memory.

Advance over the current Sewers playable-phase scene record and resume the scene-record dispatch loop.
Inputs: $02/$03 point at a valid encoded record with length/control bits in bytes +1 and +2.
Outputs: Adds the record's encoded length to $02/$03 and tail-jumps back to scene dispatch.
Clobbers: A, Y, N, V, Z, C, and $02/$03; X is preserved.
Hardware: No direct hardware-register writes; when subsequent records render, the resumed renderer updates VIC-II-visible display memory.
Advance $02/$03 to the next encoded scene record. Inputs: $02/$03 points at a valid record header. Outputs: $02/$03 points at the following record. Clobbers: A, Y, flags, and $02/$03.

Decode and render the nonterminal Sewers playable-phase scene record at $02/$03, including nested composite records.
Inputs: $02/$03 point at a non-$FF record; $1A/$1B hold its origin; relocated scene-pointer tables and renderer buffers are initialized.
Outputs: Decodes position/reflection fields, resolves child or leaf pointers, renders the record, and advances or resumes the enclosing scene tree.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, processor flags, $02-$05, $1A/$1B, $25/$26, $38, renderer scratch, and nesting stack state.
Hardware: No CIA access; descendant rendering changes VIC-II-visible bitmap, screen-code, and color memory.

Draw the picture (scene leaf) that $04/$05 point at, for the Sewers playable phase: every leaf of a scene tree falls into it from $76CD-$76D7, and DrawUiImageRecord jumps to it at $9B7C to draw a status-panel picture.
Inputs: $04/$05 point at the picture (first byte width and height nibbles, then its bitmap, screen and colour bytes); $25/$26 hold its column and row and $E8 bit 7 mirrors it; $E7/$DC are the clipping width and height; $02/$03 point at the record that placed it, whose byte 2 bits 5-6 give the number of colour-swap bytes that follow byte 2.
Outputs: Draws the visible cells into the bitmap, screen RAM, colour RAM and the colour copy at $0800, with the colour swaps applied; a picture wholly outside the window is skipped. Then it jumps to AdvanceSceneRecordAndContinue ($7641), which steps $02/$03 past the placing record and resumes the scene-record dispatch loop.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, processor flags, $02-$09, coordinate/renderer scratch, and display work memory.
Hardware: No direct hardware-register write; it stores the bitmap, screen-code and colour bytes itself, and calls the resident compositor at $1411 for cells whose colours must be merged.

Bootstrap Sewers scene, object, display, and interrupt state before gameplay setup; it builds no collision data, which CompileCollision ($A091) compiles later, from $7AAF
Inputs: resident renderer/IRQ services and the active Sewers tables and workspaces
Outputs: clears $0230, initializes scene/object work through $7C86/$7D5F/$7E6C/$80F3, sets $02A8=$FF and $C0=$FF, configures the bitmap display, and transfers through the resident IRQ-install tail
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags and all scratch/state used by the five called initializers and resident IRQ setup
Hardware: ScreenSetupVeneer programs VIC-II display registers; the tail at $1533 installs VIC/CIA IRQ state and resident vectors

Clear the play window and render The Sewers' credit/title card from six inline records. Inputs: resident play-window clear routine $140E and inline-record renderer $1583 are active; six well-formed inline records follow their calls. Outputs: the credit/title card is displayed and $7B is set to $A6. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, $7B, and renderer scratch. Hardware: changes visible display memory through resident helpers.

Text "LAST NINJA REMIX", drawn by the call at $799A that comes before it: column 7, row 2, colours $07 and $C0, then 16 glyph numbers (0 a space, 1-26 A-Z, 27-36 the digits) and a zero. The routine returns to the instruction after the zero, at $79B2.
The text routine at $1583 returns here, to the first instruction after the zero that ends "LAST NINJA REMIX" at $79B1, and the routine that called it at $799A goes on.

Text "THE SEWERS", drawn by the call at $79B2 that comes before it: column 10, row 4, colours $07 and $C0, then 10 glyph numbers (0 a space, 1-26 A-Z, 27-36 the digits) and a zero. The routine returns to the instruction after the zero, at $79C4.
The text routine at $1583 returns here, to the first instruction after the zero that ends "THE SEWERS" at $79C3, and the routine that called it at $79B2 goes on.

Text "©1990  SYSTEM 3", drawn by the call at $79C4 that comes before it: column 7, row 6, colours $07 and $C0, then 16 glyph numbers (0 a space, 1-26 A-Z, 27-36 the digits) and a zero. The routine returns to the instruction after the zero, at $79DC.
The text routine at $1583 returns here, to the first instruction after the zero that ends "©1990  SYSTEM 3" at $79DB, and the routine that called it at $79C4 goes on.

Text "WRITTEN BY JOHN TWIDDY", drawn by the call at $79E0 that comes before it: column 4, row 10, colours $07 and $C0, then 22 glyph numbers (0 a space, 1-26 A-Z, 27-36 the digits) and a zero. The routine returns to the instruction after the zero, at $79FE.
The text routine at $1583 returns here, to the first instruction after the zero that ends "WRITTEN BY JOHN TWIDDY" at $79FD, and the routine that called it at $79E0 goes on.

Text "GRAPHICS BY HUGH RILEY", drawn by the call at $79FE that comes before it: column 4, row 12, colours $07 and $C0, then 22 glyph numbers (0 a space, 1-26 A-Z, 27-36 the digits) and a zero. The routine returns to the instruction after the zero, at $7A1C.
The text routine at $1583 returns here, to the first instruction after the zero that ends "GRAPHICS BY HUGH RILEY" at $7A1B, and the routine that called it at $79FE goes on.

Text "MUSIC BY REYN OUWEHAND", drawn by the call at $7A1C that comes before it: column 4, row 14, colours $07 and $C0, then 22 glyph numbers (0 a space, 1-26 A-Z, 27-36 the digits) and a zero. The routine returns to the instruction after the zero, at $7A3A.
The text routine at $1583 returns here, to the first instruction after the zero that ends "MUSIC BY REYN OUWEHAND" at $7A39, and the routine that called it at $7A1C goes on.

EngineEntry: The Sewers' play code starts here, from PhaseHandoff at $3FF3. It sets $AA to $FF, which lets the interrupt routine play the tune, relocates the scene pointers, clears the scene buffers, waits 25 ticks, lowers the sprite curtain over the play window (AnimateStatusPanelReveal, $1F75), draws the credits card, sets the background to black, raises the curtain again and waits until it is gone (RaiseSpriteCurtain, $7C10), which shows the card, then waits for the fire button or the second button read through the SID's pot X ($D419), keeping which in $AC, and goes on into EnterArea ($7A84) and the main loop. Central Park's EngineEntry also sets $03CB to 1; this one leaves it alone.

Reinitialize the Sewers playable phase's scene buffers after GAME OVER and rejoin engine startup immediately before the common gameplay-entry tail. Its one caller is $7BD8, reached when the last life is lost and no spare life is left.
Inputs: The death sequence has finished; resident state and the active phase occupant remain valid.
Outputs: Calls the phase scene-buffer initializer, clears $D021 to black, redraws the credit/title card (RenderCreditTitleCard, $7997, which clears the play window first), and continues at the engine's input/frame-loop setup at $7A69.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, processor flags, scene/gameplay initialization state, and helper scratch.
Hardware: Writes VIC-II background color $D021 and updates display/input state through the joined engine-start tail.

Set up the current area and enter the main loop, for The Sewers. This runs once each time an area is entered or redrawn, not once a frame: it is reached by falling through from the start-up wait at $7A82, from MainTick when the redraw latch $02A9 is set ($7B34) and after a lost life ($7B9B), and it falls into MainTick ($7ADE), the per-tick loop.
Inputs: Current area $A2, the player's position and the actor/object state.
Outputs: Sets $0230=$7F; rebuilds the area's enemy meter when $012D,X holds $80-$FE and loads $022A from the area's enemy energy at $3F92; clears the play window and draws the area's scene ($8114); clears the actor slots, resets runtime state, compiles the collision records, spawns the enemy, draws inactive objects and composes the actors; on the first visit to an area below $12 sets its $011B byte and adds a score bonus ($1183 with A=$15); redraws the HUD digits, applies the area's entrance rules ($806F), stamps $026D from $E2, sets $0230=$FF and falls into MainTick.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, processor flags, $0230, gameplay zero page, actor/object/projectile arrays, renderer/collision scratch, and display work state.
Hardware: Through its helpers, writes $D021 and the VIC-II-visible bitmap, screen and colour memory.
The Sewers' own RenderConditionalSceneVariant ($8114): the plain scene, never a variant

Admit one IRQ-produced tick, run the Sewers gameplay scheduler in fixed order, and choose the next engine transition
Inputs: IRQ tick $E2 and last stamp $0268; initialized player, enemy, script, event, object, projectile, scene, and transition state
Outputs: stamps $0268; runs timing/input, player, AI, enemy animation, events, scripts, level conditions, objects, boundaries, projectiles, presentation, and resident services; then loops, restarts setup, enters death handling, or begins the level transition
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags and the union of all scheduled subsystem scratch/state
The Sewers' own ServiceEnemyBoundaryLatch: the traps in areas 4 and 10 and the guard in area 14
The Sewers adds this call for its flowing water; Central Park has no call here

Resolve the player's death in The Sewers, present the result, and select restart or GAME OVER flow. MainTick comes here when $B4 is set ($7B2A); the level exit ($02AF) goes to ResolveLevelCompletion ($7BDB), which MainTick jumps to directly
Inputs: death latch $B4, lives $03F2, spare-life flag $03E0 (item 8) and selected object $0279
Outputs: sets $0230=$7F and clears $B4, $B3 and $B6; clears the inactive-object display; LoseLife takes one from the lives; with lives left shows 'N LIVES LEFT' or '1 LIFE REMAINING' (counting the spare life), restores health, reloads the selected spawn and restarts at $7A84; with none left spends the spare life if it is held, otherwise renders GAME OVER and restarts the level through ResetSceneAfterDeath ($7A5E)
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags and renderer, delay, object and spawn scratch
Hardware: sets $D021=0 through LoseLife ($7E5E); other display changes occur through called resident/level helpers

Text "0 LIVES LEFT", drawn by the call at $7B61 that comes before it: column 9, row 8, colours $07 and $C0, then 12 glyph numbers (0 a space, 1-26 A-Z, 27-36 the digits) and a zero. The 0 at $7B68 is a placeholder: the instruction at $7B5E writes the lives left (counting the spare life) plus $1B into it before the call, so the line reads 2 LIVES LEFT or more. The routine returns to the instruction after the zero, at $7B75.
Text 7b64 plus 4, the address the instruction at $7B5E writes: byte 4 of the table at $7B64.
The text routine at $1583 returns here, to the first instruction after the zero that ends "0 LIVES LEFT" at $7B74, and the routine that called it at $7B61 goes on.

Text "1 LIFE REMAINING", drawn by the call at $7B78 that comes before it: column 7, row 8, colours $07 and $C0, then 16 glyph numbers (0 a space, 1-26 A-Z, 27-36 the digits) and a zero. The routine returns to the instruction after the zero, at $7B90.
The text routine at $1583 returns here, to the first instruction after the zero that ends "1 LIFE REMAINING" at $7B8F, and the routine that called it at $7B78 goes on.

Text "GAME OVER", drawn by the call at $7BBF that comes before it: column 10, row 8, colours $07 and $F0, then 9 glyph numbers (0 a space, 1-26 A-Z, 27-36 the digits) and a zero. The routine returns to the instruction after the zero, at $7BD0.
The text routine at $1583 returns here, to the first instruction after the zero that ends "GAME OVER" at $7BCF, and the routine that called it at $7BBF goes on.

ResolveLevelCompletion: runs when the completion request $02AF is set. In this level it asks for no items. Then it adds 5,000 points to the score ($1183 with A = $50: 5 to the thousands digit, 0 to the hundreds), takes away items 10 and 12 (clears $03E2 and $03E4), saves the items, score and clock for the next level (SaveLevelState, $1C30), counts the energy $0229 up from 0 to 21, one step each time the interrupt routine changes $022B, and jumps to the load coordinator at $16AD for the next part.

Raise the sprite curtain over the play window and wait until it is gone. Inputs: $0232 is the curtain's lower edge (a raster line, which AnimateStatusPanelReveal at $1F75 lowered) and the interrupt owns the $0231 handshake. Outputs: $0232 is reduced, two lines a frame, below $1D, sprite X expansion is disabled and $0231 is cleared, so the interrupt stops drawing the curtain. Called at the start of the game ($7A58), after a lost life ($7B95) and after GAME OVER ($7BD0). Clobbers: A, flags, $0231, and $0232. Hardware: writes VIC-II sprite X-expansion register $D01D.

Reset mutable Sewers engine state each time an area is set up: its one caller is $7AAC, in the area set-up routine that also runs at the start of play and after a lost life. Inputs: the active overlay and resident reset service. Outputs: timers, actor and object flags, arrays, and sentinels are restored to initial values. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and broad engine state. Hardware: none; the resident call (ResetEngineTickBaselines, $11F1) only copies the tick $E2 into $026C, $026E and $0277, and this body makes no direct I/O write.

Set up the status of a level as it starts. It clears $022B, $022C, $70, $89 and $A0, fills the 30 bytes at $3F92 that keep each area's enemy energy, and both energies ($0229, $022A) with $2C, a full bar, and sets $7A to $EE. It copies the item flags saved when the level began ($03B0-$03D7) over the live ones ($03D8-$03FF) and clears $03E9-$03F1 among them, then puts the score ($1CA0) and the clock's digits back from the saved copy ($03CC-$03D7). It sets $87 to $A6, clears $011B-$013E and draws panel picture 0 at both of its places (DrawUiImageRecord, $9B3D, with A = 0 and X = 0, then 1). It builds no scene or wall data. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags and the drawing routine's scratch.

Take the exit at the edge of the current area; MainTick calls it once a tick, and it does nothing while $0234 is non-zero. Inputs: $0234, current area $A2, player position $54 (across) and $55 (down), and the exit thresholds at $7DAF. Outputs: when the player is at an edge (Y below 9, Y $BD or more, X $F7 or more, or X below 2) the position becomes a place on the area's edge, counted clockwise from the top left: a quarter of the distance along the edge, plus 0 on the top, $3D on the right, $6A on the bottom and $A7 on the left. The first exit of the area's group in $7DAF whose threshold is above that place is installed through InstallSceneStateRecordX ($7D61), which moves the player to the destination area and position, or sets the level-exit request $02AF=$FF when the destination is $FF. Away from the edges it returns without change. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and the installed area/player state.

Install record 0, the level's starting place, as the selected spawn: it loads X with 0 and falls into InstallSceneStateRecordX, whatever the current room. In Sewers record 0 is area 1 at X $58, Y $5A, heading 3. Its one caller is InitSceneBuffers ($7984). Inputs: none. Outputs: $0278=0, and the area, player position, heading, command and redraw latches from record 0. Clobbers: A, X, flags, and the installed area/player state.

Install the Sewers scene-state/spawn record selected by X.
Inputs: X indexes parallel area, player-coordinate, heading, and command-state arrays at $7DCE/$7DED/$7E0C/$7E2B; callers have already resolved the transition variant and any $0234 gate.
Outputs: A $FF area byte sets $02AF=$FF and returns; otherwise stores X in $0278 and installs area $A2, player coordinates $54/$55/$028E/$028F/$74, heading $68/$69, derived pose $65, command $81, and redraw latches $02A9/$02B8.
Clobbers: A, X, processor flags, $0278, $02AF on the sentinel path, and the installed area/player/redraw state; Y is preserved.
Hardware: No direct hardware-register writes.

Load the selected Sewers spawn record into active area, player-position, facing, and transition state
Inputs: $0278 = selected record index; parallel Sewers area, X, Y, and packed facing/state tables
Outputs: $A2 = area; $54/$028E = X; $55/$74/$028F = Y; $68/$69 = heading; $65 = $10 or $11 facing-image selector; $81 = packed byte shifted right four; $02A9/$02B8 = $FF; A = $FF; X = selected index
Clobbers: A, X, and processor flags; Y is preserved

31 bytes of exit thresholds. Byte 0 belongs to no area: the scans start at byte 1, and entry 0 of the four tables that follow is the level's start position. Then comes a group for each area, closed by $FF. The routine that finds the exit the player is walking through skips a group for each area before the current one, turns the player's place on the edge of the play window into one number running clockwise round it from the top left, and takes the first value in the group above that number, the closing $FF included. The same index then selects the exit's destination in the four tables that follow.

31 exits, $7DCE-$7DEC: the area it leads to, or $FF for the way out of the level (entry 30, the closing $FF of area 14's group), which sets the level-exit request $02AF instead of moving the player. Values: 0, 1, 0, 2, 1, 4, 3, 2, 2, 5, 4, 6, 0, 5, 7, 6, 8, 7, 9, 8, 10, 11, 9, 12, 10, 11, 13, 14, 12, 13, 255.
31 exits, $7E2B-$7E49: the heading in the low three bits, and a command in the high nibble. Values: 7, 1, 5, 7, 3, 7, 1, 5, 3, 5, 1, 7, 3, 5, 1, 5, 7, 3, 7, 3, 1, 1, 5, 3, 5, 7, 1, 1, 5, 5, 255.

The player's death, once the fall is over: it clears $F2, crumbles the sprites away (DissolveSpriteImages, $9B8B), lowers the sprite curtain over the play window again (AnimateStatusPanelReveal, $1F75), waits 25 ticks (WaitEngineTicks, $9066), clears the play window ($140E), sets the background to black and takes one from the lives, item 26's flag at $03F2. The caller tests the Z flag that the DEC leaves: with no lives left it spends a spare life, item 8, if the player has one, and otherwise the game is over. Clobbers: A, X, Y and flags.
Impose a short fixed CPU delay. Inputs: none. Outputs: X ends at zero after 128 countdown iterations. Clobbers: X and flags; A and Y are preserved.

Reset The Sewers' transient control, actor, object, animation, and AI state to its fixed entry sentinels when the level starts or restarts: its one caller is InitSceneBuffers ($798B), not the area set-up. Inputs: No register arguments; the Sewers playable occupant and shared zero-page workspace are active. Outputs: Stores $FF to $6C, $02B8, and $84; stores zero to $78, $02AF, $61, $63, $64, $66, $9F, $B3, $B6, $B4, $72, $F2, $7D, $BF, and $0279; stores $F6 to $86; A returns $F6. Clobbers: A, N, and Z plus the listed RAM state; X, Y, C, and V are preserved.

Sample and normalize gameplay input and process edge-triggered interface controls for The Sewers. Inputs: active-low control-port-2 state, control-port-1/keyboard state, keyboard-select table `$1DA5`, previous edge latches, and current interface state. Outputs: `$7C` bits 0–4 from control-port-2 direction/fire and bit 5 from the POTX threshold, raw keyboard rows `$0260-$0267`, edge latches `$02AA-$02AE/$02BF`, and phase interface/action state. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and scanner/interface scratch. Hardware: writes `$FF`, keyboard-row masks, and `$80` to CIA 1 port A `$DC00`; reads `$DC00`, CIA 1 port B `$DC01`, and SID POTX `$D419`; on the F1 edge that switches the music off (`$AA` flipped to zero) it clears SID registers `$D400-$D417`.

Text "MODE  ", drawn by the call at $8002 that comes before it: column 17, row 20, colours $03 and $E6, then 6 glyph numbers (0 a space, 1-26 A-Z, 27-36 the digits) and a zero. The second space, at $800E, is a placeholder: the instruction at $7FFF writes the mode $03F3 (0 to 2) plus $1C into it before the call, so the line reads MODE 1, MODE 2 or MODE 3. The routine returns to the instruction after the zero, at $8010.
Text 8005 plus 9, the address the instruction at $7FFF writes: byte 9 of the table at $8005.
The text routine at $1583 returns here, to the first instruction after the zero that ends "MODE" at $800F, and the routine that called it at $8002 goes on.

Initial sequence byte zero and the current-value indexed base for the hidden-input recognizer at $8041. Together with the next-byte alias $805D it stores 19 values $805C-$806E; the scanner advances $BF only when normalized input matches the expected change. After the 18th matched change it sets $02AF=$FF, the request to end the level.
Expected next value of the 19-byte control sequence beginning at $805C, read with the current progress X at $8046. This is an overlapping indexed base, not another allocated array.

Apply the entrance rules for the exit the player arrived by and for the current area. Inputs: $0278, the exit record the player arrived by (an index into the tables at $7DCE on), and the current area $A2. Outputs: the entrance animation's kind and length from the list at $80DA go to $0293/$0294 (kind 0 when $0278 is not listed); exit $17 sets $74=$98 and $EF=$FF; in area $0D with item flag $03E9 set, the first collision coordinate is copied ($F2CB to $F2CD) and it returns; otherwise InitializeRoomSpecificEntranceState installs the AI scripts and sprite colours of areas $0A, $0E, $0F, $10 and $11. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and AI-script state. Hardware: writes the sprite multicolour registers $D025/$D026 directly in areas $0A, $0E, $10 and $11.

The Sewers' own entrance rules, chosen by the area number in Y: area 4 sets $F8 to 5, for the trap in that area; area 10 starts animation $B4DB in the second actor's slot and sets $F8 to 6; area 14 starts animation $B505, the guard, in the second actor's slot, sets the two sprite multicolours $D025 and $D026 to 2 and 7 (red and yellow) and sets $F8 to 7; area 5, once flag $03EC is set (item 20, taken with item 12 selected), draws object scene $A8B1, scene 79, the picture object records 4 to 6 leave once taken. Any other area returns. ServiceEnemyBoundaryLatch at $874A acts on $F8 every pass of the main loop.

The Sewers' entrance-animation list, three bytes an entry as in Central Park's (the exit the player arrived by, the kind of entrance, how many animation steps it lasts), ending with $FF: arriving by exit 0 plays kind 4 for 10 steps, and arriving by exit 11 plays kind 3 for 8 steps. ApplySceneEntryRules stores the kind and the count at $0293 and $0294, and AdvanceBoundarySequence ($887A) counts $0294 down by one each time the player's previous animation has finished, starting the next.
The second byte of each entrance-animation entry, the kind, read at $8082 with X stepping by three.

The third byte of each entrance-animation entry, its length in animation steps (AdvanceBoundarySequence counts it down once each time the player's previous animation has finished), read at $8085 with the same X.

Mark all eight actor slots inactive and clear their key state bytes. Inputs: none. Outputs: $61, $63, and the corresponding $0210 and $0248 slot arrays are cleared. Clobbers: A is zero, Y exits as $FF, and flags change; X is preserved.

Copy the 1000-byte screen-color staging image into C64 color RAM. Inputs: staging bytes $0800-$0BE7 and visible C64 I/O. Outputs: color RAM $D800-$DBE7 receives the corresponding low nybbles; the last 24 cells of the third page are harmlessly copied twice. Clobbers: A, X, and flags; X returns zero. Hardware: writes color RAM $D800-$DBE7.

Provide The Sewers' reserved per-tick runtime hook. Inputs: A normal JSR return address on the stack. Outputs: Returns immediately without changing gameplay state. Clobbers: Registers and flags are preserved; RTS consumes the normal return address.

Provide The Sewers' reserved presentation-initialization hook. Inputs: A normal JSR return address on the stack. Outputs: Returns immediately without changing presentation state. Clobbers: Registers and flags are preserved; RTS consumes the normal return address.

RTS: where The Sewers' title load points PlayNextLoadVector at $3FF6. The one call through that vector, from StartLevelLoad (engine $1405), comes once as the game starts, before any level is loaded, and goes through the engine's own JMP $0E00 there, so this RTS is never reached.
RenderConditionalSceneVariant: The Sewers draws the plain scene of the current area ($A2) every time, with none of the variants Central Park chooses with its flags.

When the player's level-condition latch is active and no player animation script is running, force zero health and install the facing-specific terminal animation
Inputs: condition latch $B6, player animation-pointer high byte $61, and facing byte $69; animation streams begin at $AA81 and $AA75
Outputs: sets player health $0229=0 and tail-installs one of the two terminal animation streams; otherwise returns unchanged

Hide the parts of an actor's sprites that are behind the current area's foreground pictures, then stage the sprites. Inputs: X is the first sprite slot to process (0 for the player, 4 for the other actor, or an auxiliary slot); it works up to slot 3, or slot 7 when X is 4 or more. A is the actor's depth ($74 or $74,X), compared with byte 1 of each 4-byte record in the area's list (pointers at $83EE, an $FF ends a list; a record is a picture's scene index, a depth, a column and a row). Outputs: for each drawn slot ($0218 bit 4 or 6 set, $0210 non-zero), every record whose depth is at least A is tested by TestSceneConditionRecord ($81F1): where the picture overlaps the 24-by-21 sprite, the sprite's pixel pairs under the picture's non-zero pixels are cleared and $0218 bit 4 is set. Then, with interrupts off, each slot with $0218 bit 6 gets its position, pointer ($30 or $38 plus the slot) and colour bits staged in $0240, $0258 and $0250, and $0210 is copied to $0248. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and masking scratch.

Mask one foreground picture out of a sprite slot. Inputs: ($ED) points at the area's list of 4-byte records (scene index, depth, column, row) and Y at the depth byte of one of them; $1F is the sprite slot, and $F4/$F6 and $F5 its X (low and high bytes) and Y. Outputs: the record's picture is placed at column x 8 and row x 8 + $1A, with the width and height from its header byte; if it does not overlap the 24-by-21 sprite the routine returns at once, otherwise it sets bit 4 of the slot's $0218 and clears, in the slot's sprite image, every pixel pair that lies under a non-zero pixel pair of the picture. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, $04-$07, $1C/$1D, $21/$22, $25/$26, $8C/$8D, $D7-$DB and the slot's sprite image.

24 entries: eight zeroes, eight ones and eight twos. $831F/$8335/$834B/$8361 use clipped horizontal pixel X to select the destination byte within a three-byte sprite row. Paired with the clearing masks at $83D5; X advances two hires pixels per multicolor source pair.

24 entries: $3F,$3F,$CF,$CF,$F3,$F3,$FC,$FC repeated for three sprite bytes. The scene-condition renderer ANDs these into the selected sprite-row byte whenever the corresponding source pixel pair is nonzero. This removes a two-bit pair, selected jointly with the byte-offset lookup at $83BD. Ends at $83EC; $83ED is a zero byte between it and the pointer directory, which no instruction reads.

ServiceEnemyBoundaryLatch, The Sewers' version, called from MainTick every pass: it does nothing while $F8 is zero, and otherwise runs the trap or guard that the entrance rules at $8095 chose for the area. $F8 = 5 is the trap in area 4 (below), 6 the one in area 10 ($879B) and 7 the guard in area 14 ($87D5).

Area 4 ($F8 = 5). When the second actor has no animation ($63 is zero) and the player's X ($54) is from $30 up to $7F, it starts animation $B48D in the second actor's slot: frame 99 appears 98 across and 28 down from where the actor stands, drops 8 pixels at a time eleven times, and then frames 100 and 101 move it 4 left and 1 down a step, over and over. Once its X ($56) is below 4 the actor is taken away: X, Y, $76 and its animation $63 are cleared, and the trap can start again. Every pass the player loses 2 energy (DamagePlayer) if they stand no more than 19 to its left or 6 to its right (the sum $56 + 6 - $54 is below 26) while its Y ($57) is $58 or more, unless the player's action, $6D with its two low bits cleared, is $0C.
no more than 19 to the left or 6 to the right?
has it come down far enough?

Area 10 ($F8 = 6). The actor that the entrance rules started with animation $B4DB (frames 102 to 104, moving 4 left and 1 down a step, over and over) is put back at the right of the area when its X is below 4: X and Y take the two bytes at $B4DE and $B4DF, which are the move of that animation's first step, $FF and $86. The player loses 2 energy if they stand within the same window across, 19 to its left to 6 to its right, and less than 16 above its Y less $48 ($57 - $48 - $55 below 16), unless their action ($6D with the low two bits cleared) is $0C.
near enough up or down?

Area 14 ($F8 = 7), the guard that the entrance rules started with animation $B505. If the player's projectile slot holds kind 7 ($0280), which is item 10 thrown once flag $03EB is set (SpawnProjectile at $9E31), with $0288 below 8, its Y ($0286) below $7A and its X ($0284) less than 32 to the right of the guard's ($56), the guard gets the animation $B55A (frames 110 to 127, ending on 127 held) and $F8 becomes 0, so nothing here runs again in this area.

Otherwise, if the player's X is at or past the guard's ($54 not below $56), the player's Y less $16 is less than the guard's Y ($57) and $02A9 is zero, it sets $B6 and $0234 to $FF: the latch DamagePlayer sets when the player's energy runs out, so the player dies.
has the player got past the guard?

AnimateWater, which The Sewers adds to MainTick (called every pass, after RenderScoreIfDirty, where Central Park has no call): the flowing water of The Sewers. Once six counts of the interrupt counter $E2 have passed since the time kept in $03E9 (the byte Central Park uses for item 17's flag), it keeps the new time and looks the current area up in the table at $8864 (sorted by area, so it stops at the first larger one). In an area with water it moves the frame $03EA on through 0, 1 and 2, writes scene $52 plus the frame into the first byte (the scene number) of that area's water placement, and draws it, so the water cycles through scenes 82, 83 and 84.
scenes 82, 83 and 84

The water in The Sewers, three bytes an entry, sorted by area and ending with $FF: the area, then the address of its water placement, a scene list whose first byte AnimateWater rewrites with scene 82, 83 or 84. Area 0: $A8B5; area 1: $A8B9; area 3: $A8BD; area 5: $A8C1; area 10: $A8C5; area 11: $A8C9; area 13: $A8CD.
The water table plus 1, read at $8841 with X at an entry's start: the low byte of the area's water placement.
The water table plus 2, read at $8846: the high byte of the area's water placement.

Script command 22, which a wall in area 6 carries (commands 5 and 6 lead here too, but no wall in The Sewers carries them): The Sewers' longer copy of ScriptRunHeading7AnimationSequence at $89C2. When the player faces heading 7 ($69) and $70 is zero, it plays animation $AB01 once (frames 73 and 74, then on into the commands of $AB06) and then $AB06 six times (frames 75, 76, 75 and 74, which take the player 11 pixels up), each to its end, 77 pixels up in all, and goes to $89EC, which sets $74 to $98 and $EF to $FF and calls ResetEngineTickBaselines. Where $89C2 plays $AB06 twice and closes with $AB1B, this has no closing animation. It clears the command $81 in every case.

Inputs: $74 and $EF as the script left them, and current actor/animation state.
Outputs: Calls $8ABD with A=4; after the bounded loop, calls RunScriptCoordinateAnimationSequence ($8B00) with X=$F8 and Y=4, which sets the player's energy $0229 to 0 and, with 8 added to $55 until it ends, runs the animation at $B442 (at $B451 when $69 + 2 has bit 2 set) and then $B460, then clears $81 and returns.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, $81, $0229, $0234, and animation/actor scratch.

When command bit 0 is set, run seven scripted cycles and enter the common death-latch tail; otherwise only clear the command.
Inputs: Command flags $81 and current actor/animation state.
Outputs: Armed path calls $8ABD with A=7 then writes $B6=$FF; unarmed path clears $81 without damage.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, $81, $0234, animation/actor scratch, and on the armed path $B6.

When command bit 0 is set, set $74, the Y the scene conditions test, to $04, hold it there with $EF = $FF, run seven cycles, and latch death.
Inputs: Command flags $81 and current actor/animation state.
Outputs: Armed path stores $74=$04/$EF=$FF and enters the seven-cycle fatal tail; unarmed path clears $81.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, $74, $EF, $81, $0234, animation/actor scratch, and on the armed path $B6.

When command bit 0 is set, set $74, the Y the scene conditions test, to $0C, hold it there with $EF = $FF, run seven cycles, and latch death.
Inputs: Command flags $81 and current actor/animation state.
Outputs: Armed path stores $74=$0C/$EF=$FF and enters the seven-cycle fatal tail; unarmed path clears $81.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, $74, $EF, $81, $0234, animation/actor scratch, and on the armed path $B6.

Run The Sewers' fixed animation at $AB4C the requested number of times, run the finishing animation at $AB61 once, then synchronize three engine-tick stamps. Inputs: A is a nonzero repetition count; animation streams $AB4C and $AB61, actor state, the blocking runtime loop, and resident tick-snapshot helper $11F1 are active. Outputs: Each $AB4C cycle is installed and serviced until $61 clears; $AB61 is then installed and serviced once; finally $026C, $026E, and $0277 receive the current engine tick $E2 and A returns that tick. Clobbers: A, X, Y, processor flags, transient stack contents, animation/runtime state, and $026C/$026E/$0277. Hardware: Through the blocking runtime loop, advances sprite/display state and reads controls; this wrapper and the $11F1 timer-snapshot tail perform no direct I/O.

Install an animation and run the blocking script runtime loop. Inputs: A:X is the animation pointer and the actor context is valid. Outputs: the animation is installed and the runtime loop completes. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and runtime state. Hardware: changes sprite presentation indirectly through the engine.

Run script-time engine frames until the active actor or action completes. Inputs: an installed animation and valid runtime state. Outputs: enemy AI, auxiliary sprites, input, and animation state advance until $61 clears. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and broad frame scratch. Hardware: changes sprite and display state indirectly and reads input through the called joystick poller.

Advance the player's and then the enemy's animation by one eligible engine step, at most once a tick. Inputs: tick $E2 and timer slot 2 ($026A, interval 1 at $8C55); both actors' animation state. Outputs: when no tick has passed since the last call the gate at $8C3F returns straight to RunScriptRuntimeLoop; otherwise AnimationInterpreter ($8F77, X=0) steps the player's animation, and ScheduleEnemyAnimation ($8F62) steps the enemy's when its own tick has advanced. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and animation scratch.

Execute a scripted action for a fixed number of completed animation cycles. Inputs: A is the repetition count and actor facing and animation state are valid. Outputs: the count is exhausted and scripted state advances. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, stack, and $0234. Hardware: changes sprite and display state indirectly.

Install one of two player-animation descriptors selected from the current facing direction. Inputs: Player facing $69 and Sewers animation descriptors $B47B and $B484. Outputs: A:X contains the selected descriptor and control tail-transfers to InstallAnimation, which initializes $60/$61, $5C, $58, $96, and $5D. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and animation state through the tail-called installer.

Script command 31. Where Central Park tests its clearance predicate here, The Sewers calls ScriptDamagePlayerTwoAndClearCommand at $8B4D, which takes two points of the player's energy, clears the command $81 and returns with A zero, so the branch to $8AF6 is always taken: X = $07 and Y = 2, then the scripted coordinate sequence at $8B00, which sets the player's energy $0229 to zero. No wall in The Sewers carries command 31, and the walls are the only source of commands, so it never runs in this level.

Script command 30. Where Central Park tests its clearance predicate here, The Sewers calls ScriptDamagePlayerTwoAndClearCommand at $8B4D, which takes two points of the player's energy, clears the command $81 and returns with A zero, so the branch to $8AFC is always taken: X = $0E and Y = 0, then the scripted coordinate sequence at $8B00, which sets the player's energy $0229 to zero. No wall in The Sewers carries command 30, and the walls are the only source of commands, so it never runs in this level.

Enter the shared temporary-Y animation sequence with offset $07 and profile index 2.
Inputs: Current Y $55, heading $69, command $81, and actor animation state.
Outputs: Clears energy/state $0229 and command $81, temporarily subtracts the offset from $55, runs profile- and heading-selected animations, then restores $55/$69.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, $55, $69, $74, $81, $0229, and animation/actor scratch; saved $55/$69 are restored.

Enter the shared temporary-Y animation sequence with offset $0E and profile index 0.
Inputs: Current Y $55, heading $69, command $81, and actor animation state.
Outputs: Clears energy/state $0229 and command $81, temporarily subtracts the offset from $55, runs profile- and heading-selected animations, then restores $55/$69.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, $55, $69, $74, $81, $0229, and animation/actor scratch; saved $55/$69 are restored.

Run the shared scripted coordinate/animation sequence selected by caller-supplied offset and profile while preserving the player's original Y coordinate and facing. Inputs: X is the temporary player-Y offset, subtracted from $55; Y (0, 2 or 4 from the callers) selects one of the six animation pointers at $8B41, 6 further on when $69 + 2 has bit 2 set; current Y $55, facing $69, and animation services $8A95/$11F1 are active. Outputs: the player's energy $0229 and command $81 are set to 0; the selected facing-adjusted animation and fixed $B460 animation run; original $55 and $69 are restored before return. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, stack, $1F, $74, $81, $0229, animation/runtime scratch, and transient $55/$69; original $55/$69 are restored.
6 words, each an animation a scripted encounter plays. Targets: $B448, $B445, $B442, $B457, $B454, $B451.
ScriptedEncounterAnimations plus 1, the address the instruction at $8B22 reads with Y as the index: the high byte of each word of the table, the index counting in pairs from the low byte.

Apply two units of player damage and consume the pending script command.
Inputs: Player energy $0229 and command $81.
Outputs: Calls DamagePlayer with A=2, then clears $81.
Clobbers: A, flags, $0229 and $81; when the energy runs out, also $6D and the death latch $B6.

Request enemy projectile type 2 through the fixed second projectile slot and consume the pending command.
Inputs: Enemy position/heading $56/$57/$6B, projectile slot 1 state $0281/$0283/$0285/$0287/$0289, and command $81.
Outputs: Passes A=2 to $9E70; if slot 1 is free and the derived coordinate is in range it initializes the slot, then clears $81.
Clobbers: A, X, flags, projectile slot-1 fields, $0296, and $81.

Request enemy projectile type 3 through the fixed second projectile slot and consume the pending command.
Inputs: Enemy position/heading $56/$57/$6B, projectile slot 1 state $0281/$0283/$0285/$0287/$0289, and command $81.
Outputs: Passes A=3 to $9E70; if slot 1 is free and the derived coordinate is in range it initializes the slot, then clears $81.
Clobbers: A, X, flags, projectile slot-1 fields, $0296, and $81.

Request enemy projectile type 4 through the fixed second projectile slot and consume the pending command.
Inputs: Enemy position/heading $56/$57/$6B, projectile slot 1 state $0281/$0283/$0285/$0287/$0289, and command $81.
Outputs: Passes A=4 to $9E70; if slot 1 is free and the derived coordinate is in range it initializes the slot, then clears $81.
Clobbers: A, X, flags, projectile slot-1 fields, $0296, and $81.

Request enemy projectile type 5 through the fixed second projectile slot and consume the pending command.
Inputs: Enemy position/heading $56/$57/$6B, projectile slot 1 state $0281/$0283/$0285/$0287/$0289, and command $81.
Outputs: Passes A=5 to $9E70; if slot 1 is free and the derived coordinate is in range it initializes the slot, then clears $81.
Clobbers: A, X, flags, projectile slot-1 fields, $0296, and $81.

Script command 41, which walls in area 5 carry (commands 35 to 40 lead here too, but no wall in The Sewers carries them): once flag $03EC is set (item 20, taken in area 5 with item 12 selected) and bit 0 of $81 is set, it clears $74 and moves the player down two pixels at a time, 16 times, composing the picture and testing the scene conditions after each step, clears $70 and leaves the area by transition variant 1 (ScriptSelectAreaTransitionVariant1).

Advance the player actor for the elapsed IRQ ticks, selecting control, script, animation, movement, collision, and logical-sprite work
Inputs: tick $E2/$026C, timed-event state $0293, player script pointer $60/$61, movement/action state $50/$51,$54/$55,$5C,$65,$68/$69,$70,$79,$89, and normalized input $7C
Outputs: stamps elapsed delta in $8F and $026C; advances timed events or control/script state; updates player coordinates, motion/pose/action, collision state, and logical sprite component buffers
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags and player-driver, movement, collision, animation, and sprite-composition scratch

Compose the player's image and hide the parts behind the area's foreground pictures. Inputs: desired direction $68 (its bit from $1DA5 goes to $1E), facing $69, frame $65, depth $74 and the current area's foreground list. Outputs: logical sprite slots 0-3 hold frame $65, mirrored for facing indexes 1 and 3 (the flags at $9196); ComposeSprites clears $9F; MaskActorSpritesBehindScenery clears the sprite pixels behind the foreground pictures and stages the slots in $0240-$025F. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, $1E, and compositor and masking scratch. Hardware: changes sprite or image RAM; no VIC-II register is written directly.

Compose the Sewers playable phase's player frame $65 into logical actor slot 0, mirrored when the facing flag at $9196,X ANDed with $1E is non-zero.
Inputs: X is the facing index ($69 shifted right once) into the four mirror flags at $9196; $1E is the direction bit of $68; $65 is the frame; player position/facing and sprite work buffers are current.
Outputs: Passes $9196,X AND $1E to ComposeSprites as the mirror flag, with X=0 and Y=$65, composes logical actor slot 0, then falls through to $8C38, which masks the player's sprites behind the area's foreground pictures.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, processor flags, sprite-composition scratch/buffers, and masking scratch.
Hardware: No direct VIC-II register write; the composition helper updates sprite work buffers and changes $01 transiently before restoring it.

Mask the Sewers playable phase's player sprites, actor slot 0, against the area's foreground pictures without recomposing its frame.
Inputs: Player sprite slots 0-3 are composed; $74 supplies the vertical coordinate compared with each foreground record's depth byte; the area's foreground list (pointers at $83EE) is current.
Outputs: Sets X=0, loads A=$74, and tail-enters MaskActorSpritesBehindScenery ($813A), which clears the sprite pixels behind the foreground pictures and stages the slots' positions, pointers and colours in $0240-$025F.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, processor flags, and masking scratch; the slots' positions are read from $0200/$0208/$0210.
Hardware: No direct hardware-register writes.

Rate-limit an update and abort its caller when the slot's minimum interval has not passed. Inputs: X timer slot (2 for the script loop's animation step, 5 for DrawActiveObject, 9 and 10 for the two auxiliary sprite slots, 12 for OpponentAI), global tick $E2, per-slot stamp $0268,X, and threshold table $8C53. Outputs: the eligible path updates timing state; the ineligible path returns to the caller's caller. Clobbers: A, flags, timing state, and two stack bytes on the abort path.

16 slot-indexed minimum intervals. $8C42 subtracts the slot's last tick $0268,X from current $E2, $8C45 compares the difference to this table and the gate discards the caller return frame when too soon; accepted calls update the saved tick. Most intervals are 1, with exceptions 6,2 and4 in the captured table; the slots this level uses are 2, 5, 9, 10 and 12, so the 2 at slot 7 is not read.

Translate the normalized Sewers input byte and current player state into facing, movement, pose, action, and animation requests
Inputs: normalized active-high control byte $7C (a set bit is a pressed direction or fire); death/condition latch $B6; player state $61,$65,$68/$69,$6C/$6D,$70,$89; decode tables at $8E11 and $8DAD
Outputs: updates desired direction $68, facing $69, action/motion $6C/$6D, pose $65, dirty flag $9F, and may select/install a player animation
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags and player-control/animation scratch

Continuation of $8C63 control interpretation: applies desired heading $68, allowing odd headings to replace $69 except an exact opposite; marks redraw $9F when changed. Sets movement $6C and derives facing/pose $65 and $6D. The $8CDC idle path clears $02B8 and may select an idle animation; $8D06 onward handles changes in the fire/action state $78, comparing direction to facing before selecting an action through $8D75. Uses $8DAD and $8E11 direction lookups; no direct hardware writes. Entry is within the larger control routine, not an independent callable API.

Translate action code A into the Sewers playable phase's player animation pointer and install that animation.
Inputs: A is the action code selected by the control logic (InterpretControls and InterpretNormalizedControls); $69 is player facing; phase animation lookup tables are valid.
Outputs: Stores A in $60, derives the facing-adjusted animation index, loads its pointer, initializes $60/$61/$5C/$58/$96/$5D, and returns.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, processor flags, $58, $5C/$5D, $60/$61, $6D, and $96.
Hardware: No direct hardware-register writes.

Install a new player animation-bytecode stream and prime its first control byte
Inputs: X = stream low byte; A = stream high byte; desired direction $68 and facing $69
Outputs: stores the stream pointer in $60/$61, loads its first byte into $5C, clears animation delay $58, copies $68 to $96, and stores $69 bit 1 in $5D
Clobbers: A, Y, and flags; X is preserved

Eight action-heading values 1,7,1,7,5,3,5,3 selected at $8D63. Index combines desired cardinal direction and current facing, then output replaces desired heading $68 before action animation selection. This is separate from the joystick low-nibble map $8E11.

Interpret the Sewers playable phase's normalized control latch and update player motion/action animation state.
Inputs: $7C is the control byte normalized by ScanAndNormalizeInput ($7E9E); player animation, action, timing, facing, and collision state are current.
Outputs: Maps the low control nybble through the direction table at $8E11; a new direction, or none, restarts the hold timer $85, sets $88=$FF and sets $6D to the facing halved; once the same direction has been held for the delay from $8E09 (4 or 8 ticks) it selects action $84 x 4 + 8 (plus $20 when $70 is 0 or 4 and up) through SelectPlayerAnimationForAction, and again at once while the player's mode class is $10. The facing $69 is read, not written.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, processor flags, player input/action/timing fields ($84, $85, $88, $6D), and animation-installation state on paths that select a new animation.
Hardware: No direct CIA or other hardware-register writes.

Eight alternating delays 4,8 indexed by normalized direction Y. $8DE2 compares elapsed tick difference against the chosen threshold before deriving action code $84*4+8, plus $20 when $70 is 0 or 4 and up, and selecting animation. This table controls action timing, not the joystick direction conversion.

16-entry map of the low four normalized control bits to eight directions 0..7 or $FF for no valid direction. $8C7C, $8D2A and $8DBA use it to choose movement/facing/action; opposing direction combinations map to $FF. Fire occupies a different input bit and is handled separately.

36 words, each one of the player's animations. Targets: $A982, $A995, $A9AA, $A9BC, $AA08, $AA19, $A96E, $A978, $AA57, $AA67, $AAEF, $AADD, $A9CE, $A9DB, $AAEF, $AADD, $AA27, $AA3F, $A96E, $A978, $A9E9, $A9F7, $A96E, $A978, $AA08, $AA19, $AAEF, $AADD, $A9CE, $A9DB, $AAEF, $AADD, $AA08, $AA19, $A96E, $A978.
PlayerAnimationPointers plus 1, the address the instruction at $8D91 reads with Y as the index: the high byte of each word of the table, the index counting in pairs from the low byte.

18 action-mode bases used at $8D7E: the action code A shifted right twice picks one, and the facing $69 shifted right once is added to it to give the player's action mode $6D, the value the control and combat code compares (as $6D with its low two bits masked) with $10, $0C and $24. The animation pointer at $8E21 is chosen separately, from A itself plus 0 or 2 for the facing. Values include $0C,$04,$18,$10,$1C,$14,$20,$28.

Build, advance, validate, and commit the player's movement candidate for this tick
Inputs: player position $54/$55 and its fractional bytes $50/$51; enemy position $56/$57; desired direction $68; facing $69; elapsed steps $8F; direction-mask table $1DA5
Outputs: initializes candidate $48-$4D and opposing position $C9/$CA, calls AdvanceCandidate, commits candidate position and fractions back to $54/$55,$50/$51, and reports vertical displacement through the shared tail at $8F3E with X=0
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags and candidate/collision scratch including $1E,$48-$4D,$C9/$CA

Build and advance the enemy movement candidate, record collision outcomes, and commit it only inside the playable bounds
Inputs: enemy position $56/$57 and its fractional bytes $52/$53; player position $54/$55; desired direction $6A; facing $6B; elapsed steps $8F; profile selector $D3; direction-mask table $1DA5
Outputs: updates candidate/collision scratch; records collision in $02B0/$02B2/$02B4 or failure count $02B1; commits $56/$57,$52/$53 only for X in [$02,$F6] and Y in [$09,$BC]; reports vertical displacement through $8F3E with X=2
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags and candidate/collision scratch including $1E,$48-$4D,$C9/$CA,$CD

Add the signed number in A to the actor's $74,X, unless $EF is set or $74,X is 0 or $FF. A positive sum is held at $FF; a negative one is not held at zero but wraps, since the BCS at $8F5D goes on to the next instruction either way. Inputs: A, and X the actor's offset. Outputs: $74,X. Clobbers: A and flags; X and Y are kept.

Run the enemy animation interpreter once when the IRQ tick has advanced
Inputs: current tick $E2, enemy animation stamp $026E, and the already-installed enemy animation stream/state at actor offset 2
Outputs: if no tick elapsed, returns unchanged; otherwise stores elapsed delta in $8F, stamps $026E, sets X=2, and tail-enters the shared animation interpreter
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, $8F, $026E, and all animation-interpreter scratch/state on the admitted path

Interpret one elapsed step of the selected actor's animation bytecode, including delay, pose, coordinate deltas, event generation, and continuation
Inputs: X=0 at $8F77 for player or X=2 at $8F79 for enemy; pointer $60/$61,X; control/delay $5C/$58-$59,X; actor position $54/$55,X; elapsed ticks $8F
Outputs: advances delay and stream position, updates pose $65,X, position $54/$55,X, event $64,X, continuation pointer, movement flags, and recomposes the actor's logical sprites when required
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags and animation, movement, event, collision, and sprite-composition scratch

Run the Sewers playable phase's animation interpreter for the scheduled enemy slot.
Inputs: X is the enemy animation-state offset selected by the scheduler (normally 2); $61,X is its stream pointer high byte; timing and animation state are current.
Outputs: Honors animation delay, decodes one bytecode step when due, updates the enemy animation/movement/event state, composes the resulting actor frame when requested, and returns.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, processor flags, $02/$03, animation timing/pointer/state bytes for slot X, actor-frame/sprite scratch, and event state selected by the bytecode.
Hardware: No direct hardware-register writes; bytecode paths requesting composition alter sprite work buffers and change CPU-port banking transiently before restoring it.

Compose an actor's current frame and hide the parts behind the area's foreground pictures. Inputs: X and $4F the actor offset (0 player, 2 enemy) and current animation frame $65,X; the mirror flag is $5D,X when $5C,X bit 4 is set, else $5C,X bit 6; depth $74,X. Outputs: the player is composed into sprite slots 0-3 with ComposeSprites, the enemy into slots 4-7 with ComposeEnemySprites; MaskActorSpritesBehindScenery then clears the sprite pixels behind the foreground pictures and stages the slots in $0240-$025F. X is not restored: it returns as 4 for the player and 8 for the enemy. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and shared renderer scratch. Hardware: it writes no chip register itself; the composer it calls switches the I/O area out through the processor port $01 while it reads the packed sprites and puts it back, and MaskActorSpritesBehindScenery stages the slots with interrupts off and ends with CLI.

Return immediately from the Sewers playable phase's animation interpreter on the shared no-further-work path.
Inputs: The preceding animation branch has completed or determined that no frame composition is needed.
Outputs: Returns to the interpreter's caller without additional state or hardware changes.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and memory are preserved; RTS advances SP by two over the caller's return frame.
Delay for the requested number of engine ticks. Inputs: A is the tick count. Outputs: the requested tick transitions have elapsed. Clobbers: A, X, flags, and wait scratch.

Advance an actor candidate by up to eight elapsed substeps and test each proposed segment against compiled collision geometry
Inputs: X = the mover's facing index ($69 or $6B shifted right once, 0-3); Y = movement-profile selector; old/candidate position $48-$4B; candidate fractional bytes $4C/$4D; direction mask $1E; elapsed count $8F
Outputs: stores profile in $027F and capped count in $8E; updates candidate coordinates; returns collision and trigger state through $23/$24,$80/$81,$CD and related movement scratch
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags and broad candidate/collision scratch

Four negative-X masks, one per facing index (the facing $69 or $6B shifted right once), read at $9081 in AdvanceCandidate. When the direction bit in $1E is in the mask, the profile's X step ($11DD,Y low, $11E7,Y high) is subtracted from the candidate X, held at 0. Values $70,$C1,$70,$C1.

Four positive-X masks, one per facing index (the facing $69 or $6B shifted right once), read at $909B in AdvanceCandidate. When the direction bit in $1E is in the mask, the profile's X step ($11DD,Y low, $11E7,Y high) is added to the candidate X, held at $FE. Values $07,$1C,$07,$1C.

Four negative-Y masks, one per facing index (the facing $69 or $6B shifted right once), read at $90B5 in AdvanceCandidate. When the direction bit in $1E is in the mask, and the horizontal guard at $918E does not match, the profile's Y step ($11E2,Y low, $11EC,Y high) is subtracted from the candidate Y. Values $07,$C1,$07,$C1.

Four positive-Y masks, one per facing index (the facing $69 or $6B shifted right once), read at $90F1 in AdvanceCandidate. When the direction bit in $1E is in the mask, and the horizontal guard at $918E does not match, the profile's Y step ($11E2,Y low, $11EC,Y high) is added to the candidate Y. Values $70,$1C,$70,$1C.

Four vertical guard masks, one per facing index (the facing $69 or $6B shifted right once), read at $90D2 and $910E in AdvanceCandidate after a Y step. When the direction bit in $1E is in the mask the same Y step is applied twice more, three times in all. All four are $11, directions 0 and 4.

Four horizontal guard masks, one per facing index (the facing $69 or $6B shifted right once), read at $90BC and $90F8 in AdvanceCandidate. When the direction bit in $1E is in the mask the Y step is skipped. All four are $44, directions 2 and 6.

Four walk-cycle masks, one per facing index (the player's facing $69 shifted right once), read at $8C01 in PlayerDriver. Each holds the three directions around that facing: $07 directions 0-2, $1C 2-4, $70 4-6, $C1 6, 7 and 0. When the direction bit in $1E is in the mask the walk frame (the low three bits of $65) steps forward by one, otherwise back by one.

Four mirror flags, one per facing index (the player's facing $69 shifted right once), read at $8C2C. The flag, ANDed with the direction bit in $1E, is passed to ComposeSprites as its mirror flag $F1, so facing indexes 1 and 3 draw the frame mirrored. Values $00,$FF,$00,$FF.

Consume and dispatch pending player and enemy animation events through the shared target-minus-one event table
Inputs: player event $64 and enemy event $66; event table begins at $91C0; X=0 selects player and X=2 enemy
Outputs: dispatches each nonzero event through the RTS table, clears $64 after the player handler and $66 after the enemy handler, and returns after both channels are empty
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, two stack bytes per dispatch, and handler-dependent state

Dispatch an event handler through a target-minus-one RTS table. Inputs: A is the event index. Outputs: control transfers to the selected handler, which returns to the original caller. Clobbers: A, Y, flags, and two transient stack bytes.

24 words, each the routine for one animation event, from event 0 up less one: the dispatcher pushes it and returns into it. Targets: $91F0, $9262, $94B2, $9267, $9282, $9287, $9E1A, $928C, $9291, $A6F8, $A6FD, $A702, $91F7, $927D, $929C, $91F1, $9282, $91F5, $91F1, $91F1, $91F1, $91F1, $896E, $91F1.
EventDispatchTable plus 1, the address the instruction at $91B7 reads with Y as the index: the high byte of each word of the table, the index counting in pairs from the low byte.
RTS: event 0 does nothing.

Events 15, 18, 19, 20, 21 and 23: load X with $FC and go on into EventPatrolGuard, which never reads X. Central Park's events of these numbers load X the same way and go on into its nudge ($AA82), which moves the player 4 left and 1 down when bit 0 of $81 is set and the player's action is not $0C; none of the animations in The Sewers' data carries them.
Event 17: loads X with 4 and goes on into EventPatrolGuard, which never reads X. No animation in The Sewers' data carries it.

Event 12, which ends each of the guard's walking animations in area 14: chooses his next walk. His direction $03ED (a byte Central Park uses for item 21's flag) becomes $FF, right, when his X ($56) is below $3C, and 0, left, when it is $8E or more; between $4C and $7D it flips at random one time in four (NextPseudoRandomByte below $40). Then it puts the next animation straight into $62/$63: walking left, $B50A (frames 106, 107, 106 and 105) when the player is $30 or more to his left, counted from 8 left of him ($56 - 8 - $54), and $B532 (frames 108, 109, 108 and 105) when the player is nearer or to the right of that; walking right, $B51E (106, 107, 106 and 105) when the player is $30 or more to the left of the point 8 right of him ($56 + 8 - $54), and $B546 (108, 109, 108 and 105) otherwise. Each step moves him 4 across and 1 up or down, and each animation ends with event 12 again.

Copy state byte $89 into actor-state byte $70 for two event codes.
Inputs: $89.
Outputs: Writes $70=$89 and returns with A equal to the copied value.
Clobbers: A and flags; $70.

Handle event 3 differently for the player channel and opponent channel.
Inputs: Actor selector X from event dispatch and current animation/AI state.
Outputs: For X=0, waits 20 engine ticks through WaitEngineTicks ($9066, A=$14), resets the tick baselines through $11F1, and sets $B4=$FF; for X!=0, sets opponent AI state $CF=$0B.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, animation/pacing scratch, and either $B4 or $CF.

Apply $2C units of player damage for event $0D.
Inputs: Player energy $0229 and existing death state.
Outputs: Tail-calls DamagePlayer with A=$2C.
Clobbers: A, flags, player energy $0229, death latch $B6, and combat scratch.

Run object mode 3 for the player, then test the combat overlap and apply the actor-to-actor hit, damage, score, and reaction result
Inputs: X = attacking actor offset (0 player, 2 enemy); this entry sets Y=3, which ObjectEngine takes as its object mode when X is 0 (TestActorCombatOverlap then overwrites Y); actor geometry/state; action modes $6D/$6F; damage tables $92D2/$92E6
Outputs: on overlap, ignores a target already in reaction $24, otherwise selects damage, calls DamagePlayer or DamageEnemy, awards score through $1187 when the player is the attacker, and latches the opposing actor's reaction
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, overlap/damage/score scratch, and object-engine state on the player channel

Resolve the selected combat-contact event. Inputs: actor state and the contact type selected by the entry path. Outputs: damage, reaction animation, collision, and object state are updated. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and combat scratch. Hardware: may change presentation or audio indirectly through damage and animation helpers.

Run object mode 5 for the player, then resolve actor overlap and dispatch the resulting player/enemy damage and reaction.
Inputs: Actor selector X (the attacker), both actors' positions/headings/animation modes, energy fields, and collision profile tables $9472-$94B1.
Outputs: Loads Y=5, which ObjectEngine takes as its object mode when X is 0 (the overlap test then overwrites Y); runs the shared overlap query, whose combat index comes from the attacker's mode $6D,X and state $70,X; on a hit applies damage to the opposing actor plus the corresponding reaction animation.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, $1E/$1F/$C5/$C6, actor animation/combat state, energy, object-engine state, and possible death/defeat persistence.

Run object mode 6 for the player, then resolve actor overlap and dispatch the resulting player/enemy damage and reaction.
Inputs: Actor selector X (the attacker), both actors' positions/headings/animation modes, energy fields, and collision profile tables $9472-$94B1.
Outputs: Loads Y=6, which ObjectEngine takes as its object mode when X is 0 (the overlap test then overwrites Y); runs the shared overlap query, whose combat index comes from the attacker's mode $6D,X and state $70,X; on a hit applies damage to the opposing actor plus the corresponding reaction animation.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, $1E/$1F/$C5/$C6, actor animation/combat state, energy, object-engine state, and possible death/defeat persistence.

Resolve the Sewers playable phase's combat overlap for attacking actor slot X, selecting the player or opponent damage and reaction path.
Inputs: X selects the attacker, actor slot 0 or the opponent slot 2; Y is the object mode for ObjectEngine; actor positions and combat state are current.
Outputs: When X is 0, runs ObjectEngine ($A704) with Y as the object mode and sets X=0 again; then runs the overlap test itself at $929C (TestActorCombatOverlap) and, on a hit, applies the matching hit/reaction/damage logic and updates actor/combat state. It returns no meaningful result.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, processor flags, combat/reaction scratch, object-engine state, and the affected actor's health/action state.
Hardware: No direct hardware-register writes.

Resolve combat overlap using the profile derived from the selected actor's current mode, then dispatch damage and reaction.
Inputs: Actor selector X plus both actors' positions, headings, animation modes, energies, and collision profile tables.
Outputs: Runs $93A6 to derive the active profile and overlap result; on a hit applies actor-specific damage and reaction animation.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, $1E/$1F/$C5/$C6, actor animation/combat state, energy, and possible death/defeat persistence.

20 attack strengths read at $92B4 for an enemy attack against the player; each is the energy DamagePlayer subtracts. Index $1F is the enemy's attack mode $6F minus $14 shifted right twice (0-3, since its attack modes are $14-$23), ORed with its profile $72 times 4 (a profile of 4 and up counts as 0), so only entries 0-15 can be read; the result enters the saturating player-damage routine $9C8B. The last four bytes ($92E2-$92E5) are not reached by this index.

16 attack values read at $92BD/$92C3 for player attacks, passed both to score accounting $1187 and the enemy-damage routine DamageEnemy ($9CA9). That routine subtracts the value from the enemy's energy $022A, held at 0: it is conventional energy subtraction, and the IRQ only moves the displayed meter $022B,X toward the energy.

Select and install the victim's hit-reaction animation. Inputs: X the victim's offset (0 player, 2 enemy); the victim's facing $69,X, mode $6D,X and energy, and the attacker's mode. Outputs: unless the victim's mode class is already $24, $6D,X is saved in $71,X and set to the facing halved plus $24. If the victim still has energy, a reaction pointer from the table at $9366, chosen by the attacker's mode and the victim's facing, is installed: for the player through InstallAnimation, with $02BD cleared, and for the enemy through InstallAiScript. If the victim's energy is 0, the player gets no new animation and $02BD is cleared, and the enemy gets the defeat script $AA81 or $AA75 (by $6B bit 2) through InstallAiScript, with $CF=7 and $0236=0. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and animation state.

32 words, each the animation the actor that is hit answers a blow with: the player's when the enemy hits them (installed with InstallAnimation), the enemy's when the player does (InstallAiScript). Targets: $AAB9, $AAB9, $AAB1, $AAB1, $AAB9, $AAB9, $AAB1, $AAB1, $AACF, $AACF, $AAA1, $AAA9, $AAA9, $AAA1, $AAC1, $AAC1, $AAB9, $AAB9, $AAC1, $AAC1, $AACF, $AACF, $AAB1, $AAB1, $AACF, $AACF, $AAB1, $AAB1, $AAB9, $AAB9, $AAC1, $AAC1.
EnemyResponseAnimations plus 1, the address the instructions at $9330 and $933F read with Y as the index: the high byte of each word of the table, the index counting in pairs from the low byte.

Test whether the selected combat actors overlap. Inputs: X selects an actor and current positions and bounds are valid. Outputs: flags and transient contact state report overlap or separation. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and overlap scratch.

Mark AI scripting active and install a new AI script pointer. Inputs: X is pointer low and A is pointer high. Outputs: $76 is set to one, $62/$63 receive the pointer, $5E/$5A are cleared, A returns zero, and X is preserved. Clobbers: A, N, Z, and AI script state; X and Y are preserved.

Install an AI script without changing the active marker. Inputs: X is pointer low and A is pointer high. Outputs: $62/$63 receive the pointer, $5E/$5A are cleared, A returns zero, and X is preserved. Clobbers: A, N, Z, and AI script state; X and Y are preserved.

Finish installing a The Sewers AI script when its low pointer byte was stored separately. Inputs: A is the script-pointer high byte and $62 already contains its low byte. Outputs: $63 receives A, $5E and $5A are cleared, and A returns zero; $62 is unchanged. Clobbers: A, N, Z, $63, $5E, and $5A; X, Y, C, V, and $62 are preserved.

16 unsigned lower horizontal bounds. $93DA-$943E derives index from attack-pose class and selected object/weapon state, then compares separation with these paired limits. $FF slots remain literal bounds; their ordinary-play reachability is open. These are combat-overlap parameters, not graphics.

16 exclusive upper horizontal bounds. $93DA-$943E derives index from attack-pose class and selected object/weapon state, then compares separation with these paired limits. $FF slots remain literal bounds; their ordinary-play reachability is open. These are combat-overlap parameters, not graphics.

16 unsigned lower vertical bounds. $93DA-$943E derives index from attack-pose class and selected object/weapon state, then compares separation with these paired limits. $FF slots remain literal bounds; their ordinary-play reachability is open. These are combat-overlap parameters, not graphics.

16 exclusive upper vertical bounds. $93DA-$943E derives index from attack-pose class and selected object/weapon state, then compares separation with these paired limits. $FF slots remain literal bounds; their ordinary-play reachability is open. These are combat-overlap parameters, not graphics.

Restore an actor's saved mode, derive its facing/pose code, and perform channel-specific follow-up.
Inputs: Actor channel offset X, current heading/mode at $69+X, saved mode at $71+X, and actor state arrays $5D/$65.
Outputs: Copies heading bit 1 to $5D+X, restores $6D+X from $71+X, derives $65+X from restored/current heading; player channel sets $9F=$FF, opponent channel rebuilds state and sets $CF=8.
Clobbers: A, X, flags, $5D+X/$6D+X/$65+X, and either $9F or opponent helper/AI state.

Admit and dispatch one active-opponent AI step, or route collision/boundary state to recovery
Inputs: active-enemy sign latch $CB; collision/boundary fields $02B0-$02B2; AI state $CF; timer slot 12; target-minus-one table beginning at $9516
Outputs: inactive enemies return; collision/boundary state jumps to recovery at $984A; admitted normal state dispatches the selected AI handler by stack/RTS
Clobbers: A, X, flags, two stack bytes, and handler-dependent state; Y is preserved until the handler

16 words, one for each state of an enemy's fighting mind from state 0 up, each the address of that state's routine less one: the dispatcher pushes it and returns into it. Targets: $9536, $9543, $95AD, $955C, $957C, $9631, $9765, $97A0, $97A5, $97E8, $97F5, $97F6, $95E4, $98F0, $0000, $960D. State 14's word is $FFFF, which would return to $0000: it is not a routine, and nothing in this load or the engine sets $CF to 14.
AiDispatchTable plus 1, the address the instruction at $950A reads with X as the index: the high byte of each word of the table, the index counting in pairs from the low byte.

Set the opponent's action mode $6F to mode class 4 plus its facing $6B shifted right once; this is AI state 0's handler in the table at $9516.
Inputs: Current opponent facing $6B.
Outputs: Stores floor(($6B + 8)/2), which is 4 + $6B/2, in $6F and returns.
Clobbers: A and flags; $6F.

Set the Sewers opponent's action mode $6F to mode class 0 plus its facing through the common tail at $953C.
Inputs: $6B is the current opponent facing/direction code.
Outputs: Computes $6F=(2*0+$6B)/2, mode class 0 plus the facing halved, and returns with it stored in $6F.
Clobbers: A, N, Z, C, and $6F; X and Y are preserved.

Set the opponent's action mode. Inputs: A is the mode class (0, 4, 8, an attack class $14-$20, or $24 for defeat) and $6B is the opponent's facing. Outputs: $6F = A + $6B/2, the class plus the facing halved, the same layout as the player's $6D. Clobbers: A, flags, and $6F.

Initialize a timed AI decision state and its random delay.
Inputs: AI option byte $D0 bit 6, tick $E2, current heading $6B, and random source $9C60.
Outputs: Sets state $CF to 3 or 4, snapshots tick to $0275, stores random delay 0..31 in $CC, and sets the opponent's action mode $6F to mode class 0 plus the facing halved.
Clobbers: A, flags, $CF, $0275, $CC, $6F, and random-source scratch.

Wait for the AI delay to expire, then enter state 5 with a rebuilt heading/action.
Inputs: Current tick $E2, delay origin $0275, delay $CC, current heading $6B, and helper state.
Outputs: Before expiry returns unchanged; at expiry sets $CF=5, derives and stores a new heading in $6A/$6B, invokes setup $9A72 with X=8, and sets the opponent's action mode $6F to mode class 8 plus the facing halved.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, $CF, $6A/$6B/$6F, and helper scratch.

Face the opponent into the player's current relative quadrant and enter approach state 5.
Inputs: Player high-byte coordinates $54/$55 and opponent high-byte coordinates $56/$57; opponent heading and action fields.
Outputs: Sets AI state $CF=5, stores the quadrant classification returned by $9A5A into both $6B (current heading) and $6A (desired heading), installs direction action class 8 through $9A72 with X=8, sets the opponent's action mode $6F to mode class 8 plus the facing halved through $953C, and returns.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, processor flags, $6A/$6B/$6F/$CF and helper scratch.

After the timed delay, choose a two-step heading turn, enter state 2, and begin horizontal-travel tracking.
Inputs: Tick/delay fields $E2/$0275/$CC, random source, heading $6B, and opponent X $56.
Outputs: At expiry sets $CF=2, rotates $6A/$6B by +2 or -2 modulo 8, snapshots $56 in $D1, runs setup X=$18, sets the opponent's action mode $6F to mode class 8 plus the facing halved, then continues into the travel tracker at $95AD.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, $CF, $6A/$6B/$6F, $D1, and helper scratch.

Track horizontal displacement from $D1, escalate after at least $14 units, and fall back to state 5 when the range test drops below $70.
Inputs: Opponent heading $6B, current X $56, baseline X $D1, tick $E2, and distance helper $9A38.
Outputs: At sufficient directed displacement sets $CF=$0C, snapshots tick, calls setup X=4, and sets the opponent's action mode $6F to mode class 0 plus the facing halved; independently, a helper result below $70 resets through the state-5 entry at $9566, which sets $CF=5 and turns $6A/$6B toward the player.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, $CF, $0275, $6A/$6B/$6F, and helper scratch.

Twelve ticks after state $0C began, enter state $0F, rotate opponent heading by two modulo 8, and rebuild movement state; it fires once, since state $0F has its own handler.
Inputs: Tick $E2, last tick $0275, heading $6B, and movement helper state.
Outputs: Before 12 ticks returns; afterward updates $0275, sets $CF=$0F, writes ($6B+2)&7 to $6A/$6B, calls setup X=4, and sets the opponent's action mode $6F to mode class 0 plus the facing halved.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, $0275, $CF, $6A/$6B/$6F, and helper scratch.

Six ticks after state $0F began, enter state 2, rotate opponent heading by two modulo 8, and rebuild movement state; it fires once, since state 2 has its own handler.
Inputs: Tick $E2, last tick $0275 (written when state $0F began, and not updated here), heading $6B, and movement helper state.
Outputs: Before 6 ticks returns; afterward sets $CF=2, writes ($6B+2)&7 to $6A/$6B, calls setup X=$18, and sets the opponent's action mode $6F to mode class 8 plus the facing halved.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, $CF, $6A/$6B/$6F, and helper scratch.

Steer the enemy toward the player. Inputs: the player's position ($54/$55) and joystick heading $68, the enemy's position ($56/$57) and heading $6B, its profile $72 and behaviour $CB, the positions kept in $028A/$028B and $028E/$028F, and the tick $E2. It aims at a point level with the player, as far to one side as the profile's entry in $9A29 says, on the side the enemy is on, judged against the player's X less 8 when $68 is 0 to 3, plus 8 when it is 4 to 7, or unchanged when $68 is negative. When that point is less than 6 away from the enemy (Manhattan distance), or when the point would fall off the screen, it goes to RetargetAiToPlayer ($966E): that keeps the player's position in $028A/$028B, faces the enemy toward the player and enters state 6. It also holds the enemy's X between 4 and $F7, retargeting when it has to.
