With $CB at $80 and the player 56 or more away, it enters state 9 when the player is at least as far from the position in $028E/$028F as the enemy is (half the X distance plus half the Y distance each), and keeps the player's position there. Otherwise, when the heading toward the point and the heading toward the player differ in bit 2, it retargets one time in 16 (a random byte below $10) if the player is less than 8 away vertically. Then it turns the enemy toward the point (a turn that changes bit 2 of the heading waits until 20 ticks have passed since the last, kept in $02BE) and sets the heading $6A from the table at $9A30: the entry before $6B when a quarter of the horizontal distance to the point is less than the vertical one, the entry for $6B when the vertical distance is under 4, and $6B itself otherwise. Outputs: $6A, $6B, $6F, $CF and the enemy's action. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, $1C-$21, $56, $028A/$028B, $028E/$028F, $02BE and the random-number state $F9-$FB.

Retarget the Sewers playable phase's opponent AI to the player's current coordinates.
Inputs: Player coordinates are $54/$55 and the enemy's are $56/$57.
Outputs: Copies $54/$55 to $028A/$028B, sets $6A/$6B to the diagonal heading from the enemy toward the player (ClassifyRelativeActorQuadrant), installs that heading's action from the table at $9AA2 (InstallAiActionByDirection with X=4), sets $6F to mode class 0 plus the heading (the heading shifted right once), sets $CF=6, and returns.
Clobbers: A, X, Y (left 0), processor flags, $1F, the enemy's animation fields $5A/$5B/$5E/$5F/$62/$63, $028A/$028B, $6A/$6B/$6F, and $CF.
Hardware: No hardware registers are read or written.

Choose between an immediate recovery/timer state and a randomized attack setup from the player's current actor mode.
Inputs: Player actor mode $6D, behavior selector $72, tick $E2, random source, opponent heading $6B, and AI sequence counter $02BD.
Outputs: If ($6D&$FC)==$24, sets $CF=8, snapshots $E2 to $0276, and stores a random byte in $D5; otherwise selects a bounded random action/setup, sets $CF=7, and increments $02BD.
Clobbers: A, X, Y (left 0 on the attack path), flags, $CF, $0276, $D5, $6F, $02BD, the random-number state $F9-$FB, and helper scratch.

Choose and install a random close-range opponent action for the Sewers playable phase.
Inputs: Opponent/player proximity tests have reached the close-range branch; the enemy's profile $72 (zero allows two variants, nonzero four), its heading $6B, animation state, and PRNG are current.
Outputs: Selects a bounded random variant, installs its animation/heading parameters through the phase helpers, sets $CF=7, increments $02BD, and returns.
Clobbers: A, X, Y (left 0), processor flags, PRNG state $F9-$FB, helper scratch, action/animation state, $CF, and $02BD.
Hardware: No hardware registers are written; each PRNG call reads CIA 1 Timer A low at $DC04 and reads high at $DC05 only on reseeding.

Wait for the opponent animation pointer high byte to clear, then initialize AI state 8 timing.
Inputs: Opponent animation pointer high byte $63, tick $E2, and random source.
Outputs: Returns while $63 is nonzero; when zero, sets $CF=8, snapshots $E2 to $0276, and stores a random byte in $D5.
Clobbers: A, flags, $CF, $0276, $D5, and random-source scratch.

Decide whether the player is close enough to the AI target for a scripted action. Inputs: player coordinates, $028A/$028B target coordinates, and AI state and timers. Outputs: proximity and action state are updated and an AI path may be entered. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and AI scratch.

Wait for both opponent animation completion and projectile slot 1 inactivity, then reset through AI state 5.
Inputs: Opponent animation pointer high byte $63 and projectile slot-1 state $0281.
Outputs: Returns if either field is nonzero; when both are zero, tail-enters the state-5 reset at $9566.
Clobbers: A, flags, and on reset A/X/Y (Y left 0) plus $CF/$6A/$6B/$6F, $1F, the enemy's animation fields and helper scratch.

Return at once, for state 10, the one enemy state that does nothing (its word in the dispatch table at $9516 is $97F4). Its RTS returns to the code that called OpponentAI: the address the dispatcher pushed at $950A-$9511 was used up by the RTS at $9512 that jumped here. Inputs and outputs: none. Clobbers: nothing.

Let a defeated enemy get up again once its energy has refilled (AI state 11, which SpawnEnemy sets for an enemy restored as defeated).
Inputs: Area index $A2, the area's defeat byte $012D,X, the ticks $E2/$F0 and the defeat time $0175,X/$0187,X, player/opponent positions $54-$57, heading $6B, and animation pointers $AA97/$AA8D.
Outputs: Returns at once while $012D,X is $FF (beaten for good). Otherwise rebuilds the enemy's energy from the ticks since its defeat (RebuildEnemyMeterFromElapsedTicks, which writes $022A and $3F92,X); when that has reached 44 and the player is not within 12 horizontally and 6 vertically, clears bit 7 of $012D,X, sets $CF=7, installs the animation at $AA97 (heading bit 2 clear) or $AA8D (bit 2 set) through InstallAiScript ($9467), and writes $0236=6; otherwise returns without transition.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, $1E/$1F, $022A, $3F92,X, and when the enemy gets up $012D,X, $CF, enemy animation state $5A/$5E/$62/$63, and $0236.
Never reached: the instruction before ends with RTS, and no instruction, branch or pointer in this load names this address.

Handle what the enemy's last move ran into.
Inputs: $02B0 is the offset of the compiled collision record the enemy's move hit (stored by MoveEnemy at $8EFF) or $FF; $02B1 counts moves that left the play area and $02B2 other blocked moves; $02B3 is the record being followed and $02A4/$02A5 the last two records hit.
Outputs: Reads $02B0 and sets it to $FF. With a record: unless it is already $02B3 it becomes $02B3, is pushed into $02A4 (the old $02A4 into $02A5) when it is not $02A4, and ChooseEnemyFacingFromContactState picks the heading, with A=2 when it equals the old $02A5 and A=0 otherwise. Then a nonzero $02B1 clears $02B1/$02B2, sets $02B3=$FF and enters state 5 (AiFacePlayerQuadrant); a nonzero $02B2 clears it, sets $02B3=$FF and retargets ($966E); otherwise it enters state $0D, clears both and runs AiTrackSelectedCollisionRecord. With $FF: when the player is less than 14 away (Manhattan) it clears $02B1/$02B2, sets $02B3=$FF and either sets $CF=5 with action mode 8 (horizontal distance under 12) or retargets; otherwise it enters state 5 when $02B1 is nonzero, or retargets.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, processor flags, $1C/$1D, $02B0-$02B3, $02A4/$02A5, $CF, and AI action/heading state on every path.
Hardware: No direct hardware-register writes.

Follow the collision record the enemy ran into (AI state $0D) and give it up when the enemy has passed it or the player comes near.
Inputs: Selected record offset $02B3 ($FF for none), the record's start and end X at $F2CB,X/$F2CD,X, opponent position $56/$57, player position $54/$55, current heading $6B, the side bit $02B5, and the tick $E2.
Outputs: Sets $02B3 to $FF and enters state 5 (AiFacePlayerQuadrant) when there is no record or the enemy's X is 8 or more below the record's start X or 4 or more above its end X; sets $02B3 to $FF and retargets at $966E when the player is less than 14 away (Manhattan distance); sets $02B3 to $FF, keeps $E2 in $02BE and enters state 5 when the enemy is heading straight away from the player, 8 or more away horizontally, and the player's vertical side matches $02B5; otherwise returns with nothing changed.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, $02B3, $02BE, $1C/$1D, $1F, $6A/$6B, $6F, $CF, and helper scratch.

Choose enemy facing and action from contact geometry. Inputs: A is 0 or 2 (2 when the record just hit is the one hit before the last), X is the previously followed record offset or $FF, and the enemy's heading $6B, the actor positions, the side bits $02B4/$02B5 and the record's byte 4 at $F2CF,$02B3 are valid. Outputs: $6A/$6B are set from the table at $99E9 (reversed when X is not $FF and $02B4 differs from $02B5), the action is reinstalled when the heading changed, action mode 8 is set, $02B5 takes $02B4, and for a record whose byte 4 AND $3E is 5 or more $6A is replaced from $99D9; a negative table entry hangs in a loop that increments the border colour. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, $1E/$1F, and AI state.

16 direction-selection bytes read at $99CB, for a record whose byte 4 AND $3E is 5 or more. The index is half the enemy's heading $6B, then bit 0 of $02B4, then whether the record's bit 6 ($40) is set, shifted in in that order. Nonnegative result becomes desired heading $6A; a negative entry takes the trap loop at $99D3, which increments the border colour $D020 for ever.

64 contact-geometry direction entries, $99E9-$9A28. $997B combines flags and selector state into Y, then $997E loads this table; negative entries take the trap, otherwise heading may be reversed and stored in $6A/$6B. A direction map for collision/AI decisions, not sprite selectors.

Seven distance offsets read at $9656/$9660 using the enemy profile $72. Added to or subtracted from player X to decide opponent approach. The following heading-map base starts at $9A30; profile bounds outside these seven values are not assumed.

Eight headings, read at $975A once the distances to the target are in $1C and $1D ($9A3A). When a quarter of $1C is less than $1D the entry read is the one before the enemy's heading $6B (the SBC #$00 at $9757 runs with the carry clear); $6B is always odd where it is set, so that is entry 0, 2, 4 or 6, a vertical heading. Otherwise, when $1D is less than 4, it is the entry for $6B itself, a horizontal heading. The entry becomes the enemy's new heading $6A, which is $6B unchanged when neither holds. The table ends at $9A37, before the Manhattan-distance routine.

Compute Manhattan distance between the engine's two coordinate pairs. Inputs: $54/$55 and $56/$57 are the two coordinate pairs. Outputs: $1C and $1D receive the absolute horizontal and vertical deltas; A is their sum saturated at $FF. Clobbers: A, flags, $1C, and $1D; X and Y are preserved.

Compute saturated Manhattan distance with the first X coordinate supplied by the caller. Inputs: A is first X and $55-$57 hold the remaining coordinates. Outputs: $1C and $1D receive the absolute horizontal and vertical deltas; A is their sum saturated at $FF. Clobbers: A, flags, $1C, and $1D; X and Y are preserved.

Classify the first coordinate pair's quadrant relative to the second: the diagonal heading from the second pair ($56/$57, the enemy) toward the first ($54/$55, the player). Inputs: $54-$57 contain the two coordinate pairs. Outputs: A is the heading 7, 5, 1 or 3 from the table at $9A6E (index bit 1 set when the first X is not less than the second, bit 0 when the first Y is not less than the second), X is that index, and $1F has the X comparison's carry shifted into bit 0. Clobbers: A, X, flags, and $1F; Y is preserved.

Classify relative quadrant with the first X coordinate supplied in A. Inputs: A is first X and $55-$57 hold the remaining coordinates. Outputs: A is the phase-table quadrant/direction code and $1F contains transient horizontal comparison state. Clobbers: A, X, flags, and $1F; Y is preserved.
The four diagonal headings 7, 5, 1 and 3: ClassifyQuadrantFromPresetX makes a number from 0 to 3 from two comparisons of X and Y positions and returns the heading it picks here.

Select and install the AI action matching the enemy's heading and an action class. Inputs: X is the action-table offset (the class); the heading is read from $6B (A is not an input), and $D3 picks the frame delay. Outputs: X is moved on by 2 when $6B is 1 or 7; $5F = $6B AND 2, $5B = the delay from $9A9E, $62/$63 = the pointer from $9AA2,X, $5E = the stream's first byte and $5A = 0. Clobbers: A, X, Y (left 0), flags, and AI script state.

Four action delays 8,6,4,4 indexed by $D3 at $9A84 and written to $5B, the enemy animation's frame delay (the interpreter copies it into the countdown $5A at each command that brings no delay of its own), before an AI action is installed.

26 words, each one of an enemy's attacking or moving animations. Targets: $A9BC, $A9AA, $9AD6, $9ADA, $9ADE, $9AF0, $9ADE, $9AF0, $9ADE, $9AF0, $9ADE, $9AF0, $9ADE, $9AF0, $A9DB, $A9CE, $A9F7, $A9E9, $AA67, $AA57, $AA3F, $AA27, $AA75, $AA81, $AA16, $AA05.
EnemyActionAnimations plus 1, the address the instruction at $9A8E reads with X as the index: the high byte of each word of the table, the index counting in pairs from the low byte.

Animation $9AD6-$9AD9, read one command a step: a control byte whose bit 1 brings a delay, a frame number, a signed X and Y move if bit 7 is set, an event if bit 0 is set, and if bit 5 is set the address to go on from (none ends it). $9AD6: control $3C, frame 17, stop.

Animation $9ADA-$9ADD, read one command a step: a control byte whose bit 1 brings a delay, a frame number, a signed X and Y move if bit 7 is set, an event if bit 0 is set, and if bit 5 is set the address to go on from (none ends it). $9ADA: control $3C, frame 16, stop.

Animation $9ADE-$9AEF, read one command a step: a control byte whose bit 1 brings a delay, a frame number, a signed X and Y move if bit 7 is set, an event if bit 0 is set, and if bit 5 is set the address to go on from (none ends it). $9ADE: control $1C, frame 8; $9AE0: control $1C, frame 9; $9AE2: control $1C, frame 10; $9AE4: control $1C, frame 11; $9AE6: control $1C, frame 12; $9AE8: control $1C, frame 13; $9AEA: control $1C, frame 14; $9AEC: control $3C, frame 15, then $9ADE.

Animation $9AF0-$9B01, read one command a step: a control byte whose bit 1 brings a delay, a frame number, a signed X and Y move if bit 7 is set, an event if bit 0 is set, and if bit 5 is set the address to go on from (none ends it). $9AF0: control $1C, frame 0; $9AF2: control $1C, frame 1; $9AF4: control $1C, frame 2; $9AF6: control $1C, frame 3; $9AF8: control $1C, frame 4; $9AFA: control $1C, frame 5; $9AFC: control $1C, frame 6; $9AFE: control $3C, frame 7, then $9AF0.

Rebuild the current area enemy meter from the 16-bit tick pair $F0:$E2 and saved tick origin $0187,X:$0175,X. Computes delta modulo 65536, shifts right five, subtracts two with a zero floor and clamps to 44. Writes both $022A and $3F92,X. The inputs are elapsed ticks, not world-height coordinates; X is current area $A2.

Draw a phase-local UI or status image record. Inputs: A is image index and X is placement variant. Outputs: the selected UI image is rendered. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, $02-$05, and renderer scratch. Hardware: reads VIC-II control state at $D011 and changes hardware-visible bitmap, screen, and color RAM.

The Sewers adds this test: when the picture is number 10 (Y holds twice the number) and flag $03EB is set, it draws it through the scene list at $9B83, which turns its white and light grey red; otherwise through $9B7F, as Central Park does.

The scene list DrawUiImageRecord points $02/$03 at for a panel picture, as Central Park's: one record, $00 $0E $0E, whose third byte has bits 5 and 6 clear, so no colour swap bytes follow, and the $FF that ends the list.

The second scene list, for item 10's picture once flag $03EB is set: the record $00 $0E $4E, whose third byte has bit 6 set, so two colour swap bytes follow: $21 (white, 1, becomes red, 2) and $2F (light grey, 15, becomes red). Then the $FF that ends the list.
Rows 3 and 9, one for each of the panel's two boxes: DrawUiImageRecord reads the row for the box in X here and draws the picture at column 33 of it.

Crumble the sprites away, then clear them: 769 passes, each ANDing one random mask from $9C5C into one random byte (0 to 63) of all 16 sprite buffers at $0C00-$0FFF, the two sets of the eight slots' images, with a short wait after each; then it clears all 1,024 bytes. The sprites on screen change because their images do. Inputs: the random-number state. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, $1E-$21 and the random-number state.

The masks $3F, $CF, $F3 and $FC, each clearing one of the four two-bit pixels of a multicolour byte. Each pass of DissolveSpriteImages ($9B97) picks one random offset from 0 to 63 and one of these masks at random, and ANDs that mask into the byte at that offset in all 16 sprite buffers at $0C00-$0FFF, so the sprites crumble a pixel at a time.

Advance and return The Sewers' table- and CIA-timer-mixed pseudo-random byte. Inputs: $F9/$FA is the readable table pointer, $FB is the previous random byte, Y is caller state to preserve, and CIA 1 Timer A is running at $DC04/$DC05. Outputs: If old $FA is at least $B6, sets $FA=($DC04 & $1F)+$75 and $F9=$DC05. Then A and $FB receive old $FB + byte[$F9/$FA] + $DC04 modulo 256, plus 1 when old $FB + byte[$F9/$FA] passes 255 (the second ADC keeps that carry); $F9 increments and $FA increments on low-byte wrap; Y is restored. Clobbers: A, N, Z, C, V, and $F9-$FB; X and Y are preserved. Hardware: Reads CIA 1 Timer A low byte $DC04 on every call and high byte $DC05 only on reseed; performs no hardware write.

Subtract unsigned A from player health $0229 with saturation at zero. Positive remaining health preserves action $6D and death latch $B6. Only the zero-result path sets $6D=($69>>1)+$24 and $B6=$FF. X/Y are preserved; no hardware registers are written.

Subtract the damage in A from the enemy's energy, keep the area's copy of it, and on defeat persist position/time state and award score
Inputs: A = unsigned damage; enemy health $022A; current area $A2; enemy position/heading $56/$57/$6B; tick/time state; defeated-count limit $D6
Outputs: stores the energy, held at 0, in $022A and in the area's copy at $3F92,$A2, which the area gets back when the player returns; on defeat awards score, records position/heading/time in $013F/$0151/$0163/$0175/$0187 indexed by area, advances bounded persistent state $012D,X, and installs reaction/action $24
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags and score/persistence/reaction scratch

Create the current area's enemy from static spawn tables or restore its persistent defeated/position record
Inputs: area index $A2; spawn/profile tables $9DC0,$9DD2,$9DE4,$9DF6,$9E08; persistent state $012D/$013F/$0151/$0163; related enemy profile fields
Outputs: initializes enemy script/motion, extents, delay, AI state, type/attributes, position, heading, action and timing fields; a zero spawn Y disables the enemy; otherwise composes its initial logical sprites
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags and enemy/script/sprite-composition state

Eight pose entries read at $9D8B. Y is half the selected enemy heading on the ordinary path and an adjusted heading on the preserved-enemy path; result goes to $67. The table is separate from the area-indexed enemy fields.
Eight mirror/auxiliary flags read at $9D90 using the same heading-derived Y as $9DB0; writes $5F. Values are zero or $FF.
18 bytes, one for each area by number, $9DC0-$9DD1: the enemy's kind in the high nibble and its profile in the low nibble. Values: 0, 32, 97, 98, 0, 0, 99, 129, 0, 130, 0, 195, 33, 193, 0, 0, 0, 0.
18 bytes, one for each area by number, $9DD2-$9DE3: the X position it starts at. Values: 0, 139, 147, 220, 0, 0, 213, 93, 0, 169, 0, 138, 87, 131, 0, 0, 0, 0.
18 bytes, one for each area by number, $9DE4-$9DF5: the Y position it starts at; 0 means the area has no enemy. Values: 0, 102, 110, 117, 0, 0, 108, 137, 0, 115, 0, 83, 93, 89, 0, 0, 0, 0.

18 bytes, one for each area by number, $9DF6-$9E07: its heading in the low three bits, and in the high nibble how many times it must be beaten before it stays down ($D6, which DamageEnemy compares with the count of its defeats at $9CE0; 15 means it always gets up again). Values: 65, 69, 67, 69, 65, 65, 71, 69, 65, 67, 65, 69, 71, 69, 65, 65, 65, 65; the high nibble is 4 in every area.

18 bytes, one for each area by number, $9E08-$9E19: its fighting style, kept in $D0, of which only bit 6 is tested (AiBeginTimedDecision, $9545: set, a timed decision goes to state 4, clear, to state 3; it is set in every area here). The low two bits, kept in $D3, also set its speed: they pick the delay, from enemy_action_delay at $9A9E (8, 6, 4 or 4), of each step of the one-frame poses and walks InstallAiActionByDirection starts (entries 2 to 13 of EnemyActionAnimations at $9AA2; the other actions bring a delay of their own in their first command, which replaces it), and, plus one, the movement profile MoveEnemy passes to AdvanceCandidate ($8EEB). Values: 65, 65, 66, 66, 65, 65, 64, 66, 65, 65, 65, 66, 67, 66, 65, 65, 65, 65.

Spawn the attacking actor's projectile into its fixed player or enemy slot after the combat-overlap precheck
Inputs: X = source actor offset (0 player, nonzero enemy); actor position/facing $54-$57/$69/$6B; player selected-object state $70/$0279/$03DC; projectile arrays $0280-$0289
Outputs: player attacks populate slot 0 only when free and allowed by selected-object state; enemy attacks populate slot 1; position, direction, lifetime, and collision stamps are initialized
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags and combat-overlap/projectile initialization scratch

Launch the enemy's projectile into slot 1 when that slot is free. Inputs: A is the projectile kind; the enemy's position $56/$57 and heading $6B. Outputs: when $0281 is free, sets the lifetime $0289 to $FF, the kind $0281 to A, the heading $0283 to $6B, the start $0285/$0287 to the enemy's position plus the heading's offsets from $A068/$A069, and $0296 to $FF; when the X offset carries the start off either side of the play area the kind is cleared to 0 and nothing is launched; when the slot is occupied nothing changes. Clobbers: A, X, flags, and projectile state; Y is kept.

Test a projectile/actor pair against the engine's two-axis collision box. Inputs: X selects projectile coordinates $0284,X/$0286,X; Y selects actor coordinates $54,Y/$55,Y. Outputs: carry is clear exactly when absolute vertical distance is below 8 and absolute horizontal distance is below 6; carry is set on either rejection. Clobbers: A and flags; X and Y are preserved.

Launch the player's projectile, in slot 0: A is its lifetime, which UpdateProjectiles counts down ($0288), and X its kind ($0280). It starts at the player's position ($54, $55) plus the offsets for the player's heading $69 from $A068 and $A069 ($0284, $0286), flies on that heading ($0282), and $0295 is set to $FF. When the X offset carries the start off either side of the play area, the kind is cleared to 0 and nothing is launched. Clobbers: A, X and flags; Y is kept.

Move the two projectile slots on by the ticks since the last call ($E2 less $0273, kept in $8F), slot 1 then slot 0, and return at once when none has passed. Each tick counts down a projectile's lifetime ($0288,X), and it is removed when that runs out. While the lifetime is 8 or more it also moves a step on its heading (the X and Y steps at $A070 and $A071), and it is removed when its X leaves 0-$FC or its Y leaves $22-$B0, or, for kinds 0 and 1, when the scenery in front has masked its sprite to nothing (bytes 1, 4 and 7 of the sprite at $0CC0 or $0EC0 for slot 0, $0DC0 or $0FC0 for slot 1, as $0295 or $0296 is 0 or not, all zero; nothing is tested while it is negative). Then a projectile of kind 0 to 5 is tested against the other side's actor (TestProjectileCollisionBox, $9EA8), unless that actor's action ($6D or $6F, the low two bits aside) is $24 or $0C: slot 1's hits the player, who loses 22 of energy (DamagePlayer, $9C8B), and slot 0's, the player's, hits the enemy while $CB is negative, which loses 44, a full bar (DamageEnemy, $9CA9). A hit starts the actor's reaction ($92F6) and removes the projectile. Kinds 6 and 7 hit nothing. Removing a projectile clears its kind ($0280,X) and its sprite's entries at $0213 and $024B for slot 0, $0217 and $024F for slot 1. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, $1E and $8F.

Sixteen bytes, one for each projectile state (the kind in the low three bits; bit 3, which the drawing routine flips every time it draws, gives the second picture): with a high byte at +16 that is not zero, the low byte of the address of an unpacked picture, otherwise the number of the packed sprite to draw. By state: sprite 0, sprite 74, $EBB2, $EBB2, $EBB2, $EBB2, sprite 74, sprite 74, sprite 0, sprite 75, $EBB2, $EBB2, $EBB2, $EBB2, sprite 75, sprite 75.
The high bytes of the same sixteen pictures; 0 means the low byte is a packed sprite number.

Sprite attribute bytes by projectile state, copied to the sprite slot's $0220 entry when it is drawn: fifteen here, -1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 6, 0, -1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 6, and state 15 (kind 7, which the player throws with item 10 selected once flag $03EB is set, on its second picture) reads the byte after them, 2, the first of the X offsets at $A05A.
X offsets from the projectile's position to where its sprite is drawn, by kind (the state's low three bits): 2, 4, 0, 0, 0, 0, 4, 4. The eighth is also the first Y offset.
Y offsets for drawing, by kind, read from here with the same index: 4, 12, 0, 0, 0, 0, 12, 12; the eighth is the first launch offset.

Where a projectile appears beside whoever throws it, by the thrower's heading h: the X offset is the byte at $A068+h and the Y offset the one after it, so the eight headings share nine bytes: 12, 18, -2, 18, 0, -8, 0, -8, -2. A launch whose X position would wrap past 0 or 255 is cancelled.
Projectile launch offsets plus 1, the address the instructions at $9E99 and $9EEB read with X as the index: the table read from its byte 1 on.

How far a flying projectile moves each step, as X and Y pairs overlapping in the same way: X at $A070+i and Y at the byte after, where i is its heading plus the offset for its kind at $A089; the furthest index reads into that table. Values: -2, 4, -1, 4, 1, -4, 1, -4, -1, 4, 0, 4, 2, -4, 2, -4, 0, 2, 2, 1, 2, -2, 2, 4, 2.
Projectile motion steps plus 1, the address the instruction at $9F9F reads with Y as the index: the table read from its byte 1 on.
The offset into the motion steps for each of the eight kinds: 0, 0, 20, 14, 16, 18, 8, 8. Kinds that share an offset fly the same way.

Expand the current area's encoded collision list into fixed six-byte segment records for movement tests
Inputs: area index $A2; concatenated $FF-terminated source lists beginning at $8593; line/slope parameters consumed by the compiler and Multiply
Outputs: emits endpoint, gradient, flags, and optional-action fields as six-byte records beginning at $F2CB and writes a zero terminator at the next record
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags and collision-compiler arithmetic/pointer scratch

Compute an unsigned 8-by-8-bit product for collision arithmetic
Inputs: X = unsigned multiplicand; Y = unsigned multiplier
Outputs: Y:X = 16-bit unsigned product
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and $45-$47

Test the candidate movement segment against the compiled collision records until one is crossed, and report the collision plus any encoded trigger
Inputs: X = heading/direction selector; old and candidate coordinates $48-$4B; movement profile $027F; six-byte records beginning at $F2CB
Outputs: returns A=$FF for collision or A=0 for none and restores X from $F3; records the matched record offset in $24 on a collision; when $027F is 0, a crossed segment with bit 0 of its flags set is a trigger: it stores the record's action byte in $80 and counts as a collision only when that byte is negative, and after the scan $81 becomes $81 plus 1 with bit 7 set
Clobbers: A, Y, flags and collision arithmetic scratch including $21-$24,$45-$47,$C5,$F3; X is restored on return

Compose the enemy's frame: the same as ComposeSprites, but with $92 set to $80 plus the enemy's profile $72 (its low two bits pick the frame's weapon part) instead of the player's weapon $70. Inputs: A is the mirror flag (stored in $F1), Y the frame number and X the first logical sprite slot (4, from $904F). Outputs: the enemy's parts are drawn into its sprite images and their positions, attributes and flags set. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and extensive compositor scratch. Hardware: changes sprite or image RAM; no VIC-II register is written directly.

Decode one actor frame descriptor into positioned logical sprite components, temporarily switching the I/O area out to read the packed sprites in the RAM under $D000-$DFFF
Inputs: A = frame attribute/modifier; Y = frame-descriptor index; X = first logical-sprite slot; actor state including $70,$7D and frame pointer tables at $AB6C
Outputs: draws the parts into the slots' sprite images ($0C00-$0FFF) and writes their positions, attributes, flags, and ready state into logical sprite arrays $0200-$0258, setting sprite-dirty state as required
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags and sprite-composition scratch including $F1,$92,$9F
Hardware: decrements then restores CPU port $01 to switch the I/O area out transiently; does not directly write VIC-II sprite registers
Never reached: the instruction before ends with JMP, and no instruction, branch or pointer in this load names this address.

Enter the Sewers playable phase's common sprite-composition body with the mode already prepared by ComposeSprites ($A301, $92 from the player's weapon $70) or by the enemy's entry at $A2F6 ($92 set to $80 plus $72).
Inputs: $F1 is the mirror flag, set when the actor faces the other way, and the low two bits of $92 pick one of a six-part frame's three alternatives; X selects the logical sprite group; Y selects the frame descriptor; CPU port $01 is in the engine's normal I/O-visible state.
Outputs: Decrements $01 for the required high-memory RAM visibility, resolves and composes the selected frame into logical sprite work buffers and the slots' sprite images, restores $01 before return, and records composition state.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, processor flags, $01 transiently, $02-$07, $1E, $42-$44, $97, $C5-$C7, $0237, $F1 on the projectile path, and logical sprite work buffers and images.
Hardware: Changes CPU-port $01 transiently by one decrement and a balancing increment to expose the required high-memory RAM; writes sprite work buffers, not VIC-II registers directly.

Finish the last slot of a composite sprite group, by marking its descriptor and restoring CPU-port banking: reached when the group's projectile slot is empty ($A400) and at the end of ConfigureCompositeSpriteSlot ($A483) after a projectile has been drawn.
Inputs: X selects the logical sprite descriptor at $0218,X; the caller entered with $01 decremented to switch the I/O area out (RAM under $D000-$DFFF).
Outputs: Sets bit 6 in $0218,X, increments $01 to restore the caller's banking state, and returns.
Clobbers: A, N, Z, $0218,X, $01, and return-address stack bytes; X and Y are preserved.
Hardware: Restores CPU-port $01 banking by one increment; no VIC-II/CIA/SID register write.

Draw a projectile into one slot of a composite actor sprite. Inputs: X is the logical sprite slot (3 or 7) and Y the projectile slot (0 or 1); the projectile's kind $0280,Y and position $0284,Y/$0286,Y are valid and $01 has been lowered by the caller. Outputs: bit 3 of $0280,Y (the image phase) is toggled; $0220,X takes the attribute from $A04B; the image is the raw one that $A02B/$A03B point at or the packed sprite they name, unpacked into $02C0; $0295 or $0296 records the buffer in use; the sprite's X ($0200, with $0208 = 0) and Y ($0210) are the projectile's position plus the kind's offsets at $A05A/$A061; $0238 and $F1 are cleared and $0271,Y takes $E2; the image is blitted into the slot's sprite, and FinishEmptyCompositeSpriteSlot sets bit 6 of $0218,X and puts $01 back. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and compositor scratch. Hardware: changes sprite metadata and RAM, and increments the processor port $01 at the end.

Consume and prepare the next component of a composite sprite definition. Inputs: $02/$03 definition pointer, Y record cursor, and X slot. Outputs: the part is decoded or configured and X and Y advance. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and part scratch. Hardware: changes sprite RAM only.

Decode a compressed 63-byte sprite and place its part. Inputs: X slot, Y record cursor, and valid compressed-stream context. Outputs: decoded cache and configured part slot are produced. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, $C5/$C6, and decoder and compositor scratch. Hardware: changes sprite RAM only.

Place one part of a frame and draw it into its sprite. Inputs: A chooses the source for the blitter (nonzero, the sprite just unpacked into $02C0; zero, the unpacked image at ($06)); $C5 the sprite slot; $C6 the part's offset in the frame record at ($02); $F1 the mirror flag and $97 the mirror width; the actor's position, $54/$55 for slots 0 to 3 and $56/$57 for slots 4 to 7. It selects the slot's sprite buffer ($A602), waits until bit 1 of the slot's flags at $0218 is clear, and sets the sprite's X ($0200/$0208: the actor's X plus the part's X offset less $30, or with $F1 set plus the mirror width less that offset), its Y ($0210, the actor's Y plus the part's Y offset) and its attributes ($0220, with bit 7, the multicolour flag, also in $0238). Then it falls into BlitSpritePartWithMask with A. Outputs: X = $C5, Y = $C6, left on the part's last byte (its attributes); A as BlitSpritePartWithMask leaves it. Clobbers: A, flags, $04/$05, $1F and $42-$44.

Draw a part into its slot's sprite at ($04), overwriting what is there: each of the 63 bytes is the source ANDed with a mask for its column ($42-$44), worked out from the sprite's X ($0200/$0208), which hides what lies past the right edge of the play window. With A nonzero the source is the sprite unpacked into $02C0 (BlitCachedSpriteMask, $A618); with A zero, the image at ($06). When the mirror flag $F1 is set the bytes go through a reversal table with the outer columns swapped: for the image at ($06), the one at $1300 (hires) or $1200 (multicolour, when bit 7 of $0238 is set); for the unpacked sprite, always $1300. Then, when the sprite's Y ($0210) is below the line in $9E, it clears that many rows from the bottom, 21 at most. Outputs: X = $C5, Y = $C6, and A 0 or the difference $0210 less $9E. Clobbers: A, flags, $1F and $42-$44.

Select the backing buffer for a sprite slot. Inputs: X is sprite-slot index and slot flags are valid. Outputs: the destination pointer is installed in compositor zero page. Clobbers: A, flags, and destination pointer; X and Y are preserved.

Copy the sprite unpacked into $02C0 into the slot's sprite at ($04), each byte ANDed with the mask for its column ($42-$44): as it is, or, when the mirror flag $F1 is set, through the bit-reversal table at $1300 with the outer columns swapped. Clobbers: A, X, Y and flags.

Resolve and expand one tokenized sprite into the fixed 63-byte decode buffer, unless the alternate $C7 mode suppresses decoding
Inputs: A = sprite index; mode byte $C7; split source-pointer tables $B6C4/$B7C4 plus base $F6C4; token stream at resolved $06/$07
Outputs: normal mode fills exactly $02C0-$02FE and returns A=$FF, X=$3F; tokens $69-$6F emit zero runs and $68 escapes a literal; alternate $C7 bit-6 mode adjusts pointer state and returns A=0 without filling the buffer
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, source pointer $06/$07, and decoder scratch

Expand a packed sprite into the 63-byte cache $02C0-$02FE from pointer $06/$07. Bytes $69-$6F emit 1-7 zeros; $68 escapes the following byte as one literal, including reserved values. Other bytes are literals. X counts output bytes; Y counts input bytes; return A=$FF. Every one of the 162 main-pool records expands to exactly 63 bytes and consumes precisely the distance to the next record.

Resolve the Sewers playable phase's alternate raw sprite pointer without decoding the 63-byte cache.
Inputs: A is the raw sprite's number; $C7 bit 6 selected raw-pointer mode before this entry.
Outputs: Stores in $06/$07 the address of that raw sprite, $EA32 plus 64 times A, returns A=0, preserves X, and leaves $02C0-$02FE unchanged.
Clobbers: A, Y, N, V, Z, C, and $06/$07; X and the 63-byte cache are preserved.

Draw projectile slot 0 into the player's fourth sprite (slot 3), at most once per tick (update slot 9 of GateUpdateByTickInterval, which returns from the caller when no tick has passed). Inputs: slot-zero state at $0280, its position $0284/$0286, and shared object and sprite state. Outputs: when $0280 is nonzero its image (the phase flipped by bit 3 of $0280) is drawn at the projectile's position and masked behind the scenery; the projectile itself is not moved. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and sprite scratch. Hardware: lowers the processor port $01 by one while it draws and puts it back; changes sprite RAM.

Draw projectile slot 1 into the enemy's fourth sprite (slot 7), at most once per tick (update slot 10 of GateUpdateByTickInterval, which returns from the caller when no tick has passed). Inputs: slot-one state at $0281, its position $0285/$0287, and shared object and sprite state. Outputs: when $0281 is nonzero its image (the phase flipped by bit 3 of $0281) is drawn at the projectile's position and masked behind the scenery; the projectile itself is not moved. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and sprite scratch. Hardware: lowers the processor port $01 by one while it draws and puts it back; changes sprite RAM.

Render the Sewers playable phase's projectile slot selected by Y into the last sprite of its group (slot 3 or 7), the common body of UpdateAuxSpriteSlot0 and UpdateAuxSpriteSlot1.
Inputs: Y is 0 for slot 0 or 1 for slot 1; $0280,Y and its position/type arrays are current; the caller's rate gate has passed.
Outputs: Returns if the slot is empty; otherwise lowers $01 to switch the I/O area out, draws the projectile into sprite slot Y*4+3 through ConfigureCompositeSpriteSlot (which puts $01 back), and tail-enters MaskActorSpritesBehindScenery ($813A) with the projectile's Y in A to hide it behind the area's foreground pictures.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, processor flags, $01 transiently, $C5-$C7, sprite work buffers, and the masking routine's scratch.
Hardware: Decrements CPU-port $01 at $A6DE and restores it in the composition helper before the tail transfer; updates sprite work buffers but does not directly write VIC-II registers.

Invoke the spatial-object engine for object subtype/channel 0.
Inputs: Current area $A2, player position/heading, object records $A811-$A881, persistence $03D8+, and event-selected channel.
Outputs: Loads Y=0 and tail-enters ObjectEngine, which filters matching records and invokes callbacks/draw state.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, $C6, $02/$03, object/animation/draw state, and callback-defined scratch.

Invoke the spatial-object engine for object subtype/channel 1.
Inputs: Current area $A2, player position/heading, object records $A811-$A881, persistence $03D8+, and event-selected channel.
Outputs: Loads Y=1 and tail-enters ObjectEngine, which filters matching records and invokes callbacks/draw state.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, $C6, $02/$03, object/animation/draw state, and callback-defined scratch.

Invoke the spatial-object engine for object subtype/channel 2.

Start the 100-tick timer of the found item shown in the panel: $A0 receives the tick $E2, or $FF when that is 0, and ExpireInactiveObjectAfterDelay ($A8FB) puts the selected item back 100 ticks later. When $A0 was 0 it first waits for raster line $FA and runs $A7CF-$A7EE, which changes its own code: with $4E = $EE, $7A/$7B = $A6EE and $86/$87 = $A6F6, the two stores at $A7D3/$A7D5 write $DD into $A7DC and $A7E4, the high bytes of SBC $0486 and CPX $04E4, so that pass reads CIA 2's timers through mirrors ($DD24, $DD86, $DDE4); the stores at $A7EC/$A7EE put $04 back, and the results of the reads are not kept. Inputs: $A0, tick $E2, pointers $7A/$7B and $86/$87, and $4E. Outputs: $A0. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and $A0. Hardware: reads VIC-II raster register $D012 and CIA 2's timer registers; writes no hardware register.

25-byte instruction continuation of $A7C4, including undocumented LAX absolute,Y at $A7D7. With Y = $4E = $EE, LAX loads both A and X from $DD24 (CIA 2's timer A low, through a mirror). The stores at $A7D3/$A7D5 have just changed the high bytes of the next two instructions ($A7DC and $A7E4) from $04 to $DD, so SBC $0486 and CPX $04E4 run as SBC $DD86 and CPX $DDE4 (CIA 2's timer B low and timer A low); each selects whether an optional BIT $75A1 runs. Every path reaches LDA #4 and stores it through $7A/$86 at Y, which puts $04 back in $A7DC and $A7E4. The comparisons change the path and its timing, not the stored value.

End of raster-synchronized object-state update: read the tick $E2, replace zero with $FF, save it as the active-object timestamp $A0, then return. The following $A7F9-$A810 bytes are a pointer table; they are not instructions.

6 words, each a point inside one of the player's two pick-up animations ($AADD and $AAEF): the command after each of the three that raise events 9, 10 and 11, which run the object engine with actions 0, 1 and 2. After an object is taken (and when a record's routine returns with Y = $FF), the object engine compares the player's animation pointer $60/$61 with them; on a match it moves the pointer to the word beside it in PickupAnimationReplacements and doubles the countdown $58. Targets: $AAE1, $AAE4, $AAE7, $AAF3, $AAF6, $AAF9.
PickupAnimationMatches plus 1, the address the instruction at $A7AA reads with X as the index: the high byte of each word of the table, the index counting in pairs from the low byte.

6 words, each the point in the same pick-up animation that the player's animation pointer ($60/$61) is moved to when it holds the word beside it in PickupAnimationMatches: the first of each three moves it on to the animation's last command and the second to the one before, and the third and sixth are the same as their matches, so there only the doubled countdown $58 changes anything. ObjectNeedsItem12: the routine object records 4 to 6 (area 5) call before their object can be taken. It compares the selected item $0279 with 12 and returns with Z set, which lets the take go ahead, only when item 12 is selected. The take sets item 20's flag $03EC, which opens the way down in area 5 (the entrance rules at $8095 and command 41 at $8B6D).

ObjectUseItem10: the routine object record 7 (area 13) calls before its object can be taken. Only with item 10 selected ($0279) does it go on (otherwise Z is clear and nothing is taken): it sets flag $03EB to $FF, draws picture 10 again in the panel's second box (X = 1), which DrawUiImageRecord now draws in red, and clears item 10's flag $03E2. It returns with Y = 10 and Z set, so ObjectEngine goes on with item 10 in place of the record's item 19: it sets $03E2 again, adds 500 points to the score ($1183 with A = 5, the hundreds digit) and draws picture 10 once more. Item 19 is never taken; its flag $03EB is the one this routine sets, which also keeps the record from matching again. Item 10 stays selected, and thrown with $03EB set it flies as projectile kind 7, the one that stops the guard in area 14.

The RTS that ends the Sewers playable phase's inactive-object expiry check. The branches at $A902 and $A906 come here when the delay has not elapsed or no inactive object is pending, and ClearInactiveObjectAndRefreshUi also ends here after redrawing the panel's image.
Inputs: A valid return address is on the stack.
Outputs: Returns; on the two branch paths nothing has been cleared or redrawn.
Clobbers: Registers, flags, object state, and memory are preserved; RTS advances SP by two over the caller's return frame.

Inputs: timer slot 5; phase counter $A9; current area $A2; 14-byte records at $A811; persistent active bytes $03D8,Y; two active scene pointers in record bytes 5-6 and 7-8

Eight pointers, one for each kind of extra sprite the enemy can carry: none, $D1E9, $D1E9, $D1E9, $D999, $E1C1, $E1C1, $EA32. The extra sprite is part of the enemy's figure, not its weapon (the weapon is the frame's alternative slot, picked by the low two bits of $92): for frames 0 to 48, the frames the pose table at $D1B8 covers, the composer draws it in the enemy's first sprite, in place of the frame's first slot and at the position of its second, and sets the attributes of the enemy's first three sprites from $D1A8; for frames 45 and 46, whose pose entries are $FF, it draws nothing in that sprite. The high nibble of the area's entry in the enemy table at $9DC0 picks the pointer: it is twice the kind, a byte offset into this table. The composer adds a word offset taken from the pose table to the chosen pointer, reads the word there and unpacks the image it leads to, the same way for every kind. No area's enemy has a kind whose pointer is $EA32, the unpacked images.
